guide.bcd.restore_security.general.s6: Still the same error after the restart? Try VTDiag's 'Reinstall Vanguard cleanly' guide.
guide.bcd.restore_security.general.text: Use this when Vanguard shows VAN 25, 128 or 193 and you're not sure what changed. These commands only put back Windows' normal security settings.
guide.bcd.restore_security.hypervisor_of: Open an admin Command Prompt: press Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator. Click Yes.
Paste this and press Enter. It puts back the Windows default.
Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
Then make sure Memory integrity is on (VTDiag's 'Turn on Memory Integrity' guide).
Windows is set to never start its hypervisor. Memory Integrity and Vanguard's security checks need it. This is often left over from old emulator or VM tweaks.
guide.bcd.restore_security.nx_off.s1: Open an admin Command Prompt: press Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator. Click Yes.
guide.bcd.restore_security.nx_off.s2: Paste this and press Enter. 'OptIn' is the Windows default.
guide.bcd.restore_security.nx_off.s3: Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
guide.bcd.restore_security.nx_off.s5: If the error stays, check that 'NX Mode' (AMD) or 'Execute Disable Bit' (Intel) is Enabled in the BIOS.
guide.bcd.restore_security.nx_off.text: Data Execution Prevention (NX) is turned off in the Windows boot settings. Windows normally keeps it on, and Vanguard needs it.
guide.bcd.restore_security.outcome: After the restart, did the Vanguard error go away?
guide.bcd.restore_security.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.bcd.restore_security.summary: Turns off test mode and other developer boot options that Vanguard doesn't allow (VAN 25, 128, 193). These are Riot's own official steps. About 2 minutes plus a restart.
guide.bcd.restore_security.testsigning_o: Open an admin Command Prompt: press Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator. Click Yes.
Paste this and press Enter. You should see 'The operation completed successfully.'
Paste this one too. If Windows says the value is protected by Secure Boot policy, that's fine; just skip it.
Paste this to turn off kernel debugging as well.
Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
Let VTDiag check that test mode is off.
If an app asked you to turn test mode on, it won't work with Vanguard. Uninstall it if you don't need it.
Windows 'test mode' is on (you may see 'Test Mode' in the corner of the desktop). It lets unsigned drivers load, so Vanguard refuses to run. Some mod tools and old drivers turn it on.
guide.bcd.restore_security.title: Restore Windows security settings
guide.bios.update.desktop.s1: Find your motherboard model: Start > type 'System Information' > 'BaseBoard Manufacturer' and 'BaseBoard Product'. VTDiag's report shows it too.
guide.bios.update.desktop.s2: On the maker's own website, open the support page for exactly that model and download the newest BIOS. Read its notes; very old BIOS versions sometimes need a middle version first.
guide.bios.update.desktop.s3: Save your BitLocker key, then Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Suspend protection. When everything is done, click Resume protection if it didn't come back on by itself.
guide.bios.update.desktop.s4: Unzip the download and copy the BIOS file to an empty USB stick (FAT32). Plug it into a USB port on the back of the PC.
guide.bios.update.desktop.s5: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.bios.update.desktop.s6: Open the flash tool: {flash_tool}. Pick the file from the USB stick and start.
guide.bios.update.desktop.s7: Don't turn off the PC or press any button while it runs. It can take 5-10 minutes and restart a few times; that's normal.
guide.bios.update.desktop.s8: Settings are usually reset now. Turn Secure Boot ({secureboot}), TPM ({tpm}) and XMP/EXPO for your RAM back on, then press F10 and choose Yes.
guide.bios.update.desktop.text: On desktop PCs you update the BIOS with the flash tool built into the motherboard, from a USB stick.
guide.bios.update.flash_failed.s1: Wait at least 30 minutes without touching anything. Some updates show a black screen for a long time and restart several times. Turning the PC off in the middle of an update can break it.
guide.bios.update.flash_failed.s2: Still nothing after 30 minutes and no lights or fan changes? Turn the PC off with the switch on the power supply (or hold the power button), wait a minute and turn it on again.
guide.bios.update.flash_failed.s3: Look in the motherboard manual for 'BIOS FlashBack', 'Dual BIOS' or 'BIOS recovery'. Many boards can restore the BIOS from a USB stick with a special button.
guide.bios.update.flash_failed.s4: If the PC starts but settings look odd, choose 'Load Optimized Defaults' in the BIOS, then turn Secure Boot and TPM back on.
guide.bios.update.flash_failed.s5: If nothing works, contact your PC or motherboard maker's support. They can usually repair a failed BIOS update.
guide.bios.update.flash_failed.text: The PC doesn't start after the update, or the update stopped halfway? Stay calm and don't keep pressing buttons. This is usually fixable.
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.s1: Find your exact model: Settings > System > About, or the sticker under the laptop. On Dell, also note the Service Tag.
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.s2: Get the update from your maker. On your PC that's: {flash_tool}
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.s3: Download the newest BIOS for exactly your model and read its notes. Some very old BIOS versions must be updated in steps.
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.s4: Save your BitLocker key, then Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Suspend protection. When everything is done, click Resume protection if it didn't come back on by itself.
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.s5: Plug in the charger, close all apps and run the update. The PC restarts by itself, maybe several times.
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.s6: Don't turn it off, close the lid or unplug it while it runs, even if the screen stays black for a few minutes.
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.s7: Afterwards, check that Secure Boot and TPM are still on (run a VTDiag scan, or in the BIOS: {secureboot}).
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.s8: Let VTDiag check the BIOS version.
guide.bios.update.laptop_or_prebuilt.tex: On laptops and prebuilt PCs, the maker gives you a BIOS update made for your exact model. It usually runs from Windows.
guide.bios.update.outcome: Did the update finish, and is the problem gone?
guide.bios.update.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.bios.update.pre.1: Plug in the charger first. A BIOS or firmware update must never run on battery power.
guide.bios.update.summary: Installs the newest motherboard firmware, which fixes many Secure Boot, TPM, IOMMU and Vanguard crash problems. About 20-30 minutes. It usually goes fine if you follow every step, but losing power during the update can break the motherboard, so only do it when it's really needed and keep the PC plugged in.
guide.bios.update.title: Update your BIOS
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.s1: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.s2: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.s3: Open the boot order (Boot > Boot Option Priorities, or 'Boot Sequence') and set 'Windows Boot Manager' as #1. Linux entries (GRUB, ubuntu, shim) go after it.
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.s4: Make sure Secure Boot stays Enabled. Usually here: {secureboot}
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.s5: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.s6: To start Linux later, use the one-time boot menu (often F8, F11 or F12 right after power-on) instead of changing the order again.
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.s7: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check Secure Boot.
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.s8: If Windows Boot Manager sits on the Linux drive, or VAN 1 stays, fixing boot files is an advanced job. Back up your files and ask Riot support or someone experienced.
guide.boot.dualboot.dualboot.text: VTDiag found another operating system's boot entry. If Linux or GRUB starts first, or Secure Boot is off for Linux, Vanguard can't verify that Windows started securely (VAN 1).
guide.boot.dualboot.general.s1: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.boot.dualboot.general.s2: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.boot.dualboot.general.s3: Open the boot order (Boot > Boot Option Priorities, or 'Boot Sequence') and set 'Windows Boot Manager' as #1. Linux entries (GRUB, ubuntu, shim) go after it.
guide.boot.dualboot.general.s4: Make sure Secure Boot stays Enabled. Usually here: {secureboot}
guide.boot.dualboot.general.s5: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.boot.dualboot.general.s6: To start Linux later, use the one-time boot menu (often F8, F11 or F12 right after power-on) instead of changing the order again.
guide.boot.dualboot.general.s7: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check Secure Boot.
guide.boot.dualboot.general.s8: If Windows Boot Manager sits on the Linux drive, or VAN 1 stays, fixing boot files is an advanced job. Back up your files and ask Riot support or someone experienced.
guide.boot.dualboot.general.text: VTDiag didn't detect a second system, but if you ever installed Linux or another OS on this PC, the same steps apply.
guide.boot.dualboot.outcome: Did VALORANT start without VAN 1 / the Secure Boot error?
guide.boot.dualboot.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.boot.dualboot.summary: Fixes VAN 1 and Secure Boot errors on PCs with Linux (or another system) installed next to Windows. About 5-10 minutes in the BIOS.
guide.boot.dualboot.title: Put Windows first in the boot order
guide.clock.fix.general.s1: Open Settings > Time & language > Date & time.
guide.clock.fix.general.s2: Turn on 'Set time automatically', then click 'Sync now'.
guide.clock.fix.general.s3: If the clock is wrong again after every restart, the small battery on the motherboard (CMOS) may be empty. A PC shop can replace it cheaply.
guide.clock.fix.general.text: Make sure Windows keeps the time right by itself.
guide.clock.fix.outcome: Does the Riot Client log in now?
guide.clock.fix.skewed.s1: Let VTDiag sync the clock with Microsoft's time server.
guide.clock.fix.skewed.s2: Open Settings > Time & language > Date & time.
guide.clock.fix.skewed.s3: Turn on 'Set time automatically' and 'Set time zone automatically'.
guide.clock.fix.skewed.s4: Check that the time zone shown is where you live, then restart the Riot Client.
guide.clock.fix.skewed.text: Your PC clock is more than 5 minutes off.
guide.clock.fix.summary: A wrong date, time or time zone breaks secure connections, so the Riot Client and Vanguard can't connect. About 2 minutes.
guide.clock.fix.title: Set your PC clock right
guide.discord.stream_audio.discord.s1: In Discord, open User Settings (gear) > 'Voice & Video'.
guide.discord.stream_audio.discord.s2: Scroll to the screen share part and find 'Use an experimental method to capture audio from applications'.
guide.discord.stream_audio.discord.s3: Switch it (off if it's on, on if it's off), then restart Discord.
guide.discord.stream_audio.discord.s4: When you Go Live, pick the VALORANT window under 'Applications' and make sure 'Sound' is on.
guide.discord.stream_audio.discord.s5: Black stream? Set VALORANT to 'Windowed Fullscreen' in Settings > Video > General.
guide.discord.stream_audio.discord.text: Discord has a setting for how it grabs sound from apps.
guide.discord.stream_audio.obs.s2: Under Sources, click '+' > 'Application Audio Capture' and pick VALORANT.
guide.discord.stream_audio.obs.s4: Stream from OBS to where your friends watch, or right-click the OBS preview > 'Windowed Projector' and share that window in Discord.
guide.discord.stream_audio.obs.text: A workaround with OBS (free). It takes a bit of fiddling.
guide.discord.stream_audio.outcome: Stream again. Can your friends hear the game now?
guide.discord.stream_audio.summary: When you stream VALORANT on Discord and friends can't hear the game or its voice chat, it's usually a Discord capture setting. About 5 minutes.
guide.discord.stream_audio.title: Get game sound into your Discord stream
Go Live, open the 'Screens' tab and pick your main screen.
Make sure 'Sound' is on. Mute music or videos you don't want friends to hear.
Sharing your whole screen sends all PC sound except Discord itself.
guide.display.settings.game.s1: In VALORANT Settings > Video > General, set 'Display Mode' to 'Fullscreen'.
guide.display.settings.game.s2: Set 'Resolution' to your monitor's real size (for example 1920 x 1080) with the right refresh rate.
guide.display.settings.game.s3: Stuck in a wrong mode? Press Alt+Enter to switch, then set it again.
guide.display.settings.game.s4: In Settings > System > Display, use the resolution marked '(Recommended)'.
guide.display.settings.game.s5: Under 'Advanced display', pick the highest refresh rate your monitor supports.
guide.display.settings.game.s6: Two monitors? Click the one you play on and tick 'Make this my main display'.
guide.display.settings.game.text: Check the resolution and display mode in the game and in Windows.
guide.display.settings.gsync.s1: NVIDIA Control Panel > Display > 'Set up G-SYNC' > tick 'Enable G-SYNC, G-SYNC Compatible' > Apply.
guide.display.settings.gsync.s2: With G-Sync on, you can set 'Vertical sync' to 'On' in 'Manage 3D settings'. Never use 'Fast'.
guide.display.settings.gsync.s3: In VALORANT, turn V-Sync off and set 'Limit FPS Always' a little under your refresh rate (for example 141 for 144 Hz, 237 for 240 Hz).
guide.display.settings.gsync.text: For a smooth, tear-free picture on a G-Sync or G-Sync Compatible monitor. This is optional; if it feels worse, turning G-Sync off is fine too.
guide.display.settings.monitor_off.s1: Right-click the Start button and choose 'Device Manager'.
guide.display.settings.monitor_off.s2: Open 'Monitors'. Right-click any entry with a small down arrow > 'Enable device'.
guide.display.settings.monitor_off.s3: In Settings > System > Display > 'Multiple displays', click 'Detect'.
guide.display.settings.monitor_off.text: A monitor that doesn't show up at all may be switched off in Device Manager.
guide.display.settings.nvidia_app.s1: Open the NVIDIA app > Settings and turn off automatic optimization of newly added games.
guide.display.settings.nvidia_app.s2: Under 'Graphics', open VALORANT and don't press 'Optimize'.
guide.display.settings.nvidia_app.s3: Set the resolution in VALORANT again.
guide.display.settings.nvidia_app.text: The NVIDIA app can 'optimize' games and set a wrong resolution (for example 4K).
guide.display.settings.nvidia_vsync.s1: Right-click the desktop and open 'NVIDIA Control Panel' (on Windows 11 click 'Show more options' first).
guide.display.settings.nvidia_vsync.s3: Set 'Vertical sync' to 'Use the 3D application setting' and click Apply.
guide.display.settings.nvidia_vsync.s4: On the 'Program Settings' tab, pick VALORANT if it's listed and check the same setting there.
guide.display.settings.nvidia_vsync.text: NVIDIA's 'Fast' V-Sync setting is known to crash VALORANT with 'A critical error has occurred'.
guide.display.settings.outcome: Start VALORANT. Is the picture sharp and smooth, without the error?
guide.display.settings.replay.s1: Before you watch a replay, set 'Limit FPS Always' to about 360 (lower on a weaker PC).
guide.display.settings.replay.s2: Set it back after you're done.
guide.display.settings.replay.text: Replays can stutter or crash at very high FPS.
guide.display.settings.summary: Wrong resolution, a blurry picture, tearing or a crash with 'A critical error has occurred' often come from display settings in the game or the graphics driver. 5 to 10 minutes.
guide.display.settings.title: Fix wrong resolution, blur and tearing
guide.display.stretched_res.amd.s1: Open AMD Software and go to Settings (gear) > Display.
guide.display.stretched_res.amd.s2: Turn 'GPU Scaling' on and set 'Scaling Mode' to 'Full panel'.
guide.display.stretched_res.amd.s3: Under 'Custom Resolutions', click 'Create New' (accept the note).
guide.display.stretched_res.amd.s4: Type the width and height you want, keep your refresh rate and click 'Save'.
guide.display.stretched_res.amd.s5: Now set it in the game (see the 'in game' part).
guide.display.stretched_res.amd.text: On AMD, use AMD Software: Adrenalin.
guide.display.stretched_res.cru.s1: Download CRU from its official page (ToastyX on monitortests.com) and unzip it into a new folder.
guide.display.stretched_res.cru.s2: Run CRU.exe. Under 'Detailed resolutions', click 'Add', type your size, keep the refresh rate and click OK.
guide.display.stretched_res.cru.s3: Click OK again, then run 'restart64.exe' from the same folder to apply it.
guide.display.stretched_res.cru.s4: To undo everything, run 'reset-all.exe' and then 'restart64.exe'.
guide.display.stretched_res.cru.s5: If the screen stays black after a change, start Windows in Safe Mode and run 'reset-all.exe'.
guide.display.stretched_res.cru.text: Only if your graphics panel won't make the resolution. CRU (Custom Resolution Utility, by ToastyX) is free.
guide.display.stretched_res.in_game.s1: In VALORANT Settings > Video > General, set 'Display Mode' to 'Fullscreen'.
guide.display.stretched_res.in_game.s2: Pick your new resolution and set 'Aspect Ratio Method' to 'Fill'.
guide.display.stretched_res.in_game.s3: Black bars? Switch 'Display Mode' to 'Windowed' and back to 'Fullscreen'.
guide.display.stretched_res.in_game.s4: Don't edit VALORANT's config files (like GameUserSettings.ini) or make them read-only to force a stretch. Players got their accounts suspended for tricks like that.
guide.display.stretched_res.in_game.s5: Riot sometimes changes how stretched resolutions work in a patch. If it broke right after an update, the cause may not be on your side.
guide.display.stretched_res.in_game.text: Set it in VALORANT, and stay away from config-file tricks.
Open Intel Graphics Command Center > Display.
Add a 'Custom resolution' with the size you want and keep your refresh rate.
Now set it in the game (see the 'in game' part).
On Intel graphics, use Intel Graphics Command Center (free in the Microsoft Store).
guide.display.stretched_res.nvidia.s1: Right-click the desktop and open 'NVIDIA Control Panel'.
guide.display.stretched_res.nvidia.s2: Go to Display > 'Adjust desktop size and position'. Pick 'Full-screen' and set 'Perform scaling on' to 'GPU'.
guide.display.stretched_res.nvidia.s3: Tick 'Override the scaling mode set by games and programs' and click Apply.
guide.display.stretched_res.nvidia.s4: Go to Display > 'Change resolution' > 'Customize...' > 'Create Custom Resolution'.
guide.display.stretched_res.nvidia.s5: Type the size you want (for example 1440 x 1080 or 1280 x 960), keep your refresh rate, click 'Test' and then 'Yes'.
guide.display.stretched_res.nvidia.s6: Now set it in the game (see the 'in game' part).
guide.display.stretched_res.nvidia.text: On NVIDIA, the scaling and the custom resolution are both in NVIDIA Control Panel.
guide.display.stretched_res.outcome: Start a Deathmatch. Does the stretched resolution fill the screen now?
guide.display.stretched_res.summary: A stretched resolution (like 1440 x 1080 on a wide monitor) is made with your graphics card's control panel, not with game file tricks. About 10 minutes.
guide.display.stretched_res.title: Set up a stretched resolution the safe way
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.s1: Press Start, type 'environment' and open 'Edit the system environment variables'. Click Environment Variables.
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.s2: Look at the lower list (System variables). Only add what's missing; don't delete or change anything else.
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.s3: If 'ComSpec' is missing: click New, type ComSpec as the name and paste this as the value.
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.s4: If 'TEMP' or 'TMP' is missing in System variables: click New, name it TEMP (or TMP) and paste this as the value.
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.s5: In the upper list (User variables), TEMP and TMP should point here. Add them the same way if they're missing.
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.s6: If 'Path' is missing completely: click New, name it Path and paste this as the value. If Path exists, select it > Edit and add only the missing parts with New, one per line.
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.s7: Click OK in every window, then restart the PC.
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.s8: Let VTDiag check the variables again.
guide.env_vars.restore.broken.text: VTDiag found that some basic Windows variables are missing. Vanguard needs them, for example to save its logs ('Failed to create zip archive').
guide.env_vars.restore.general.s1: Press Start, type 'environment' and open 'Edit the system environment variables'. Click Environment Variables.
guide.env_vars.restore.general.s2: Look at the lower list (System variables). Only add what's missing; don't delete or change anything else.
guide.env_vars.restore.general.s3: If 'ComSpec' is missing: click New, type ComSpec as the name and paste this as the value.
guide.env_vars.restore.general.s4: If 'TEMP' or 'TMP' is missing in System variables: click New, name it TEMP (or TMP) and paste this as the value.
guide.env_vars.restore.general.s5: In the upper list (User variables), TEMP and TMP should point here. Add them the same way if they're missing.
guide.env_vars.restore.general.s6: If 'Path' is missing completely: click New, name it Path and paste this as the value. If Path exists, select it > Edit and add only the missing parts with New, one per line.
guide.env_vars.restore.general.s7: Click OK in every window, then restart the PC.
guide.env_vars.restore.general.s8: Let VTDiag check the variables again.
guide.env_vars.restore.general.text: Use this if Vanguard can't save its logs, or apps say they can't find their temp folder.
guide.env_vars.restore.outcome: After the restart, does Vanguard work (and save its logs) again?
guide.env_vars.restore.summary: Puts back basic Windows settings (TEMP, TMP, Path, ComSpec) that some cleaner tools remove, which breaks Vanguard and other apps. About 5-10 minutes plus a restart.
guide.env_vars.restore.title: Restore missing Windows environment variables
guide.gpu.clean_driver.amd.s1: Go to amd.com > Drivers & Support and pick your graphics card.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.amd.s2: If the newest driver started the problem, open 'Previous Drivers' on that page and download an older version that worked well for you, or one players call stable.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.amd.s3: Close VALORANT and the Riot Client.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.amd.s4: Run the installer and tick 'Factory Reset' under 'Additional Options'. This removes the old driver and its settings first.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.amd.s6: In AMD Software, set update checks to manual for now, so it doesn't jump back to the newest version.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.amd.s7: While you test, leave AFMF, RSR and Anti-Lag off for VALORANT.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.amd.text: New AMD Software: Adrenalin versions sometimes bring freezes or black screens. Going back to an older version that was stable is a normal fix.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.ddu.s1: First download DDU from its official site (Wagnardsoft) and the new driver. Save both on the desktop.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.ddu.s2: Disconnect from the internet (unplug the cable or turn Wi-Fi off). This stops Windows from installing its own driver in the middle.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.ddu.s3: Open Settings > System > Recovery. Next to 'Advanced startup', click 'Restart now'.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.ddu.s4: Choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings > Restart, then press 4 for Safe Mode. If BitLocker asks for a key, enter the key you saved.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.ddu.s5: In Safe Mode, open DDU. Choose 'GPU' and your brand (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel), then click 'Clean and restart'.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.ddu.s6: Back in normal Windows, still offline, run the driver installer you downloaded.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.ddu.s7: Restart, then connect to the internet again.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.ddu.text: Only if a normal clean install didn't help. DDU (Display Driver Uninstaller) is a free tool that removes every trace of the old driver. It usually goes fine if you follow these steps; take your time. On a laptop with two graphics chips, remove only the driver of the brand that has the problem, and if the brand's installer refuses, use the driver from your laptop maker's support page.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.intel_other.s1: Intel: download the free 'Intel Driver & Support Assistant' from intel.com, let it scan and install the graphics driver.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.intel_other.s2: Laptop? If Intel's installer refuses, get the graphics driver from your laptop maker's support page instead.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.intel_other.s3: Not sure which card you have? Open Device Manager > 'Display adapters' to see the name.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.intel_other.s5: Never use 'driver updater' programs or random driver sites. Only nvidia.com, amd.com, intel.com or your PC maker.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.intel_other.text: Intel graphics, or not sure what you have? Use the official tools only.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.nvidia.s1: Go to nvidia.com > Drivers, pick your graphics card and download the 'Game Ready' driver. Only download from nvidia.com.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.nvidia.s2: Close VALORANT and the Riot Client.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.nvidia.s3: Run the installer and choose 'Custom (Advanced)' install.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.nvidia.s4: Tick 'Perform a clean installation' and click Next.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.nvidia.s5: The screen may go black or flicker for a moment. That's normal.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.nvidia.s6: Restart your PC when it's done.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.nvidia.s7: Did the newest driver make things worse? On nvidia.com, use the driver search to get the version before it and install it the same way.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.nvidia.text: You have an NVIDIA graphics card. NVIDIA's installer has a clean-install option built in.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.outcome: Play a match. Are the crashes, black screens or low FPS gone?
guide.gpu.clean_driver.pre.0: VALORANT is still running. Close the game and the Riot Client first.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.pre.1: BitLocker is on. If you use the Safe Mode (DDU) part, Windows may ask for your BitLocker recovery key. Save it first: click Start, type 'Manage BitLocker', open it and choose 'Back up your recovery key'.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.summary: A broken or buggy graphics driver can cause crashes, black screens or very low FPS. Installing a fresh driver from the official site with the clean-install option fixes most of these. 15 to 30 minutes.
guide.gpu.clean_driver.title: Do a clean graphics driver install
guide.gpu.igpu.bios_auto.s1: Open these steps on your phone first, because the PC screen will be in the BIOS. Change only the setting named here.
guide.gpu.igpu.bios_auto.s2: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If the BIOS doesn't open, restart and press {key} again and again while the PC starts.
guide.gpu.igpu.bios_auto.s3: Find 'Integrated Graphics' (it may be called 'iGPU', 'IGD' or 'UMA'). It's often under 'Advanced' or 'Chipset'.
guide.gpu.igpu.bios_auto.s5: Press F10 to save and exit, then confirm with 'Yes'.
guide.gpu.igpu.bios_auto.s6: If the PC doesn't start normally, go back into the BIOS and set it back the way it was.
guide.gpu.igpu.bios_auto.text: Some AMD Ryzen PCs freeze when the built-in graphics is turned off in the BIOS. Setting it to 'Auto' helped players, even with the monitor on the graphics card. It uses a little RAM (about 512 MB).
guide.gpu.igpu.cable.s2: At the back, the motherboard's video ports sit up high next to the USB ports. The graphics card's ports are lower, in a horizontal row.
guide.gpu.igpu.cable.s3: Move the monitor cable to a port on the graphics card (HDMI or DisplayPort).
guide.gpu.igpu.cable.text: Your monitor is plugged into the motherboard, so your graphics card isn't drawing the picture.
guide.gpu.igpu.disabled.s1: Right-click the Start button and choose 'Device Manager'.
guide.gpu.igpu.disabled.s2: Open 'Display adapters'. A switched-off entry has a small down arrow (for example 'AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics' or 'Intel UHD Graphics').
guide.gpu.igpu.disabled.text: The built-in graphics is switched off in Device Manager. Some PCs freeze when it's off.
guide.gpu.igpu.hybrid.s1: Let VTDiag tell Windows to always run VALORANT on the graphics card.
guide.gpu.igpu.hybrid.text: Your PC has two graphics chips. Windows may run VALORANT on the weaker built-in one.
guide.gpu.igpu.intel_old.s1: Download the free 'Intel Driver & Support Assistant' from intel.com and let it update the graphics driver.
guide.gpu.igpu.intel_old.s2: If it refuses, use the newest graphics driver from your laptop maker's support page.
guide.gpu.igpu.intel_old.text: Your Intel graphics driver is old. On Intel laptops this often causes freezes after a match starts.
guide.gpu.igpu.no_driver.s1: Right-click the Start button and choose 'Device Manager'.
guide.gpu.igpu.no_driver.s2: Open 'Display adapters' and 'Other devices'. Look for a yellow mark or 'Microsoft Basic Display Adapter'.
guide.gpu.igpu.no_driver.s3: AMD Ryzen: on amd.com > Drivers & Support, pick your processor and install the 'Chipset' driver and the graphics driver for it.
guide.gpu.igpu.no_driver.s4: Intel: use the free 'Intel Driver & Support Assistant' from intel.com.
guide.gpu.igpu.no_driver.s5: Laptop: get the chipset and graphics drivers from the laptop maker's support page.
guide.gpu.igpu.no_driver.s6: Restart and check that no yellow marks are left in Device Manager.
guide.gpu.igpu.no_driver.text: Windows shows a graphics chip without a driver ('Microsoft Basic Display Adapter' or a yellow mark). On AMD Ryzen PCs this can freeze the whole PC.
guide.gpu.igpu.outcome: Play for a while. Did the freezes stop, and does VALORANT run on your graphics card?
guide.gpu.igpu.summary: A built-in graphics chip without a driver, switched off, or used instead of your graphics card can cause freezes or low FPS. Most fixes take 5 to 15 minutes; one needs the BIOS.
guide.gpu.igpu.title: Fix built-in graphics problems
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.bios_driver: An old BIOS causes freezes on many new AMD and Intel PCs. Follow the guide 'Update your BIOS' (guide.bios.update).
Install the chipset driver from AMD, Intel or your motherboard maker.
Updated the graphics driver lately? Try a clean install of the one before (guide.gpu.clean_driver).
Everything at default and it still freezes? A part may be faulty, so get help from the shop or maker (warranty) and show them the VTDiag report.
Old firmware and drivers can also freeze new PCs.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.optical.s2: Restart the PC and start VALORANT.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.optical.s3: Plug it in only when you need it, and not while you play.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.optical.tex: A USB CD/DVD/Blu-ray drive is plugged in. Some of these make the PC restart when VALORANT starts.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.outcome: Play normally for a day or two. Did the freezes and restarts stop?
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.power_usb.s: Let VTDiag stop Windows from putting USB ports to sleep. This helped some players with freezes.
Turn off the PC. Check that the graphics card's power cables are pushed in fully at both ends.
Unplug USB devices you don't need: hubs, card readers, disc drives, cheap adapters. Test with only mouse, keyboard and headset.
Plug the PC straight into the wall, not into a cheap power strip.
A weak or old power supply can switch the PC off under load. If it only happens in games, compare its watts with what your graphics card maker recommends.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.power_usb.t: The power supply, loose cables and USB devices are common causes too.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.ram_oc.s1: Undo any overclock in programs like MSI Afterburner or Ryzen Master (click 'Reset' or 'Default').
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.ram_oc.s2: Open these steps on your phone first, because the PC screen will be in the BIOS. Change only the setting named here.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.ram_oc.s3: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If the BIOS doesn't open, restart and press {key} again and again while the PC starts.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.ram_oc.s4: Find 'XMP', 'EXPO' or 'DOCP' (often on the first BIOS page, or under 'Ai Tweaker' or 'OC') and set it to 'Disabled'.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.ram_oc.s5: If you turned on 'PBO', 'Curve Optimizer' or a CPU overclock, set those to 'Auto' or 'Disabled' too.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.ram_oc.s6: Press F10 to save and exit, then confirm with 'Yes'.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.ram_oc.s7: Play normally for a day or two. If the freezes stop, the RAM settings were unstable: keep XMP off, or try again after a BIOS update.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.ram_oc.text: RAM profiles (XMP, EXPO or DOCP) and overclocks make the PC faster, but if they're unstable the whole PC freezes. Turning them off for a test is safe, and you can turn them on again later.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.realtek.s1: Let VTDiag switch off the network port you don't use. Your Wi-Fi keeps working.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.realtek.tex: You play on Wi-Fi, but a wired Realtek network port is switched on. Its driver has caused whole-PC freezes for some players.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.summary: When the whole PC freezes, restarts or logs 'Kernel-Power 41', the cause is usually hardware: heat, unstable RAM settings, the power supply or a USB device. These free checks go from easy to harder; change one thing at a time.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.temps.s1: Download HWiNFO (free) from its official site (hwinfo.com). Open it and choose 'Sensors-only'.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.temps.s2: Leave it open, play a match, then look at the 'Maximum' column.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.temps.s3: Check 'CPU Package' (or 'CPU (Tctl/Tdie)') and 'GPU Temperature'. Staying at 95 °C or more for the processor, or 90 °C or more for the graphics card, is too hot.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.temps.s4: Too hot? Turn off and unplug the PC, then clean dust from the fans and filters (hold the fans still while you blow).
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.temps.s5: More tips are in the guide 'Fix overheating' (guide.hardware.thermal).
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.temps.text: 'Kernel-Power 41' only means the PC lost power without shutting down cleanly; it's a sign, not the cause. Heat is the easiest thing to check first, with the free tool HWiNFO.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.title: Find out why the whole PC freezes or restarts
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.whea.s1: First, turn off XMP/EXPO and any overclock for a test (see the 'RAM and overclock' part).
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.whea.s2: Update the BIOS with the guide 'Update your BIOS' (guide.bios.update).
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.whea.s3: Test your RAM: click Start, type 'Windows Memory Diagnostic', open it and choose 'Restart now and check for problems'.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.whea.s4: If errors continue with everything at default, a part may be faulty. If it's under warranty, contact the shop or maker and show them the VTDiag report.
guide.hardware.freeze_checks.whea.text: Windows logged hardware errors (WHEA). These come from the processor, RAM, graphics card or motherboard, not from VALORANT.
guide.hardware.thermal.desktop.s1: Download HWiNFO (free) from hwinfo.com, open 'Sensors-only', play a match and check the 'Maximum' column.
guide.hardware.thermal.desktop.s2: Processor staying at 95 °C or more, or graphics card at 90 °C or more, is too hot.
guide.hardware.thermal.desktop.s3: Turn off and unplug the PC. Clean dust from the fans, filters and the graphics card (hold fans still while you blow).
guide.hardware.thermal.desktop.s4: Check that every fan spins when the PC is on.
guide.hardware.thermal.desktop.s5: Front fans should pull air in; back and top fans should push it out.
guide.hardware.thermal.desktop.s6: Keep the case away from walls and out of closed cabinets.
guide.hardware.thermal.desktop.text: On a desktop PC, check temperatures and airflow.
guide.hardware.thermal.fps_over_time.s1: When the FPS drops, check temperatures in HWiNFO.
guide.hardware.thermal.fps_over_time.s2: In VALORANT Settings > Video > General, use 'Fullscreen' instead of 'Windowed Fullscreen'.
guide.hardware.thermal.fps_over_time.s3: Set 'Limit FPS Always' near your monitor's refresh rate. Less FPS you can't see means less heat.
guide.hardware.thermal.fps_over_time.s4: Set 'Limit FPS in Menu' and 'Limit FPS in Background' low (like 30 to 60).
guide.hardware.thermal.fps_over_time.tex: FPS that is fine at first and drops after 10 to 20 minutes is a typical heat sign.
guide.hardware.thermal.laptop.s1: Plug in the charger. Many laptops run much slower on battery.
guide.hardware.thermal.laptop.s2: Use the laptop on a desk, not on a bed, pillow or your lap. The air vents underneath need space.
guide.hardware.thermal.laptop.s3: Lift the back by 1 to 2 cm (a book works), or use a cooling pad.
guide.hardware.thermal.laptop.s4: Clean the vents: shut down, unplug, and blow short bursts of air into the vents.
guide.hardware.thermal.laptop.s5: A few years old and still hot? A repair shop can clean the inside and renew the thermal paste, but this costs money.
guide.hardware.thermal.laptop.s6: Set the maker's performance mode too (see 'Make your laptop run at full speed', guide.power.laptop_mode).
guide.hardware.thermal.laptop.s7: Vanguard (vgc) looks heavy on a hot laptop because the processor slows down. Players saw it drop after cleaning the fans.
guide.hardware.thermal.laptop.text: Laptops have small fans and get hot fast. A few simple changes make a big difference.
guide.hardware.thermal.outcome: Play for 30 minutes. Does your FPS stay steady now?
guide.hardware.thermal.summary: When a PC gets too hot it slows itself down to stay safe. FPS that drops after a while, or Vanguard (vgc) using lots of CPU on a laptop, are typical signs. Cleaning and airflow fix most of it. 10 to 30 minutes.
guide.hardware.thermal.title: Fix overheating
guide.hvci.enable.cannot_comply.s1: Install all Windows updates and restart. Some Memory Integrity fixes come through Windows Update.
guide.hvci.enable.cannot_comply.s2: Update the BIOS (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide). New versions sometimes add missing virtualization options.
guide.hvci.enable.cannot_comply.s3: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) > Performance > CPU. If 'Virtualization' is missing or your BIOS has no such option, the processor may not support it.
guide.hvci.enable.cannot_comply.s4: Contact Riot support with your VTDiag report (VTDiag's 'Contact Riot support' guide) and tell them what you tried.
guide.hvci.enable.cannot_comply.s5: Don't use tools or scripts that claim to fake or bypass these checks. They break Riot's rules and can get your account banned.
guide.hvci.enable.cannot_comply.text: If you tried the parts above and Memory Integrity still won't run, your PC may not be able to meet this requirement (for example a very old processor, or a BIOS without virtualization). That's not something you did wrong.
guide.hvci.enable.configured_not_running: Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
Let VTDiag check that Memory Integrity is running.
Still not running? Open Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation details. If it warns about an incompatible driver, use the 'incompatible drivers' part.
Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
Make sure virtualization is Enabled: {virtualization}. Press F10 and choose Yes.
Back in Windows, let VTDiag check again.
Memory Integrity is switched on, but it isn't running yet. Usually it just needs a restart; otherwise CPU virtualization is off in the BIOS.
guide.hvci.enable.incompatible_drivers.s: Open Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation details. Click 'Review incompatible drivers' and write down the names (they end in .sys).

Find which app or device each one belongs to by searching the file name online. Common owners: old RGB lighting tools, old anti-cheats of other games, fan or monitor tools, old audio or Wi-Fi drivers.
Update that app from its maker's site. If you don't need it, uninstall it: Settings > Apps > Installed apps.
For an old audio or Wi-Fi driver, install the newest one from your PC or motherboard maker's support page.
Don't delete .sys files from Windows folders yourself. That can break devices or stop Windows from starting.

Two known cases: ene.sys (RGB lighting tools, e.g. old ASUS Aura versions) and se64a.sys (monitor tools like softOSD). Uninstall the app that owns them first; for leftovers, follow Riot's own support article for that file.
Restart, then turn Memory integrity On in Core isolation and restart once more.
Let VTDiag check. If a driver still blocks it and you can't find its app, contact Riot support and include the driver names.
guide.hvci.enable.incompatible_drivers.t: Windows won't turn on Memory Integrity because an old driver is in the way. Drivers come with an app or a device, so the fix is to update or remove that app, not to delete files.
guide.hvci.enable.off.s1: Open Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation details.
guide.hvci.enable.off.s2: Turn Memory integrity On. If Windows asks for permission, click Yes.
guide.hvci.enable.off.s3: If the switch is grey or Windows lists incompatible drivers, use the 'incompatible drivers' part of this guide.
guide.hvci.enable.off.s4: Restart the PC when Windows asks.
guide.hvci.enable.off.s5: Let VTDiag check that Memory Integrity is running.
guide.hvci.enable.off.s6: Start VALORANT. If the Riot Client offers to repair files, let it.
guide.hvci.enable.off.text: Memory Integrity is off. It's a normal Windows security setting and takes a minute plus a restart. On some older PCs it costs a few FPS, but Vanguard needs it on your PC.
guide.hvci.enable.outcome: Is Memory Integrity on, and does VALORANT start now?
guide.hvci.enable.summary: Fixes VAN RESTRICTION 5 / VAN 9005 when Vanguard needs Memory Integrity (Core isolation) running. Usually 5-15 minutes plus a restart; longer if an old driver is in the way.
guide.hvci.enable.title: Turn on Memory Integrity
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.s1: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.s2: If the BIOS opens in a simple screen, switch to 'Advanced Mode' (often F7 or F2).
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.s3: Set virtualization to Enabled. Usually here: {virtualization}
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.s4: If you see 'Execute Disable Bit' (Intel) or 'NX Mode' (AMD), make sure it's Enabled too.
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.s5: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.s6: Back in Windows: open Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation details and turn Memory integrity On.
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.s7: Restart the PC when Windows asks.
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.s8: Let VTDiag check that Memory Integrity is running.
guide.hvci.enable.virt_off.text: Memory Integrity needs CPU virtualization, and it's switched off in your BIOS. Turn that on first, then Memory Integrity.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.auto.s1: Let VTDiag remove saved priority settings for Riot programs. You can undo it in VTDiag.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.auto.text: Some tweaks save an 'always High priority' setting for Riot programs. VTDiag can remove it.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.ecores.s1: Open Settings > System > Power and set 'Power mode' to 'Balanced' or 'Best performance', not a power-saving mode.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.ecores.s2: Keep Windows updated. Windows 11 knows these processors best.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.ecores.s3: Close heavy background apps while you play (browser videos, recording, downloads), so the fast cores stay free.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.ecores.s4: Don't turn off E-cores in the BIOS or use affinity tricks. They rarely help and can cause VAN errors.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.ecores.s5: A BIOS update often improves these processors (guide.bios.update).
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.ecores.text: Intel 12th-gen and newer processors have fast P-cores and smaller E-cores. With normal settings, Windows puts the game on the fast cores by itself.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.outcome: Restart your PC and play a match. Are the VAN errors and freezes gone?
Open Process Lasso and find VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe, VALORANT.exe and vgc.exe.
Right-click each one and remove its 'Always' rules for CPU priority and CPU affinity.
Easier: uninstall Process Lasso from Installed apps. Its rules go away with it.
Turn off 'game booster' features in other tools (ParkControl, cleaners) too.
Process Lasso and similar 'booster' tools keep priority rules saved, so they come back every time.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.summary: Forcing VALORANT, Vanguard or Discord to 'High' or 'Realtime' priority can cause VAN 136 / VAN 185 errors and freezes. Windows handles priority well on its own. About 5 minutes.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.task_manager.s: Don't set VALORANT, vgc or Discord to 'High' or 'Realtime' in Task Manager > Details > 'Set priority'.
Set it before? It resets when you close the game, so just don't set it again.
If you really want to change it, 'Above normal' is the highest that players found safe.
Don't change 'Set affinity' for vgc.exe (Vanguard). Leave Vanguard alone.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.task_manager.t: Priority set by hand in Task Manager.
guide.hybrid_cpu.priority.title: Put game priority back to normal
guide.iommu.enable.drivers_after.s1: Download the newest audio and Wi-Fi drivers from your PC or motherboard maker's support page, not from random driver sites.
guide.iommu.enable.drivers_after.s2: Install them and restart the PC.
guide.iommu.enable.drivers_after.s3: No sound? Open Sound settings and pick your speakers or headset as the output device again.
guide.iommu.enable.drivers_after.s4: If the PC keeps crashing at start, open the BIOS ({key}) and set IOMMU back to Auto only to get into Windows. Update the drivers, then turn it on again.
guide.iommu.enable.drivers_after.s5: Using an Ethernet cable instead of Wi-Fi can help for now, while you wait for a better Wi-Fi driver.
guide.iommu.enable.drivers_after.s6: Still broken? Contact Riot support with your VTDiag report.
guide.iommu.enable.drivers_after.text: Sound or Wi-Fi stopped working, or the PC crashes, after you turned IOMMU on? That's usually an old audio or Wi-Fi driver that doesn't work well with IOMMU.
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.s1: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.s2: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.s3: If the BIOS opens in a simple screen, switch to 'Advanced Mode' (often F7 or F2).
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.s4: Set IOMMU / VT-d to Enabled (not Auto). Usually here: {iommu}
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.s5: If you also see 'DMA Protection', 'DMAr Support', 'Pre-boot DMA' or 'Kernel DMA Protection', set them to Enabled. Check that virtualization is on too: {virtualization}
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.s6: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.s7: Once Windows has started, shut the PC down fully once and turn it on again. Some boards only apply this setting after a full power-off.
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.s8: Let VTDiag check again. 'Kernel DMA Protection: Off' in System Information is usually fine; Vanguard checks the BIOS setting.
guide.iommu.enable.enable_in_bios.text: IOMMU lets the PC control which devices may read memory directly. It's a BIOS setting (Intel calls it VT-d, AMD calls it IOMMU or AMD-Vi), and on your PC it looks switched off.
guide.iommu.enable.on_but_still_error.s1: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.iommu.enable.on_but_still_error.s2: Check that IOMMU / VT-d is Enabled, not Auto: {iommu}. Press F10 and choose Yes.
guide.iommu.enable.on_but_still_error.s3: Update the BIOS to the newest version (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide). Riot asked many players to do this because board makers released a security fix for it.
guide.iommu.enable.on_but_still_error.s4: After the update, check the IOMMU setting again. BIOS updates often reset it.
guide.iommu.enable.on_but_still_error.s5: If the error stays, contact Riot support with your VTDiag report.
guide.iommu.enable.on_but_still_error.te: Windows already sees IOMMU working. If Vanguard still asks for it, or says 'update motherboard firmware', your BIOS most likely needs an update.
guide.iommu.enable.option_missing.s1: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.iommu.enable.option_missing.s2: Look under Advanced, Chipset, 'AMD CBS > NBIO Common Options' or 'System Agent'. On your PC it's usually here: {iommu}
guide.iommu.enable.option_missing.s3: Not there? Update the BIOS (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide) and look again.
guide.iommu.enable.option_missing.s4: Laptop or prebuilt PC (for example some HP Victus models)? If even the newest BIOS has no such option, ask the maker's support whether one is coming.
guide.iommu.enable.option_missing.s5: Contact Riot support with your VTDiag report and your PC model. Sometimes waiting for a Vanguard or BIOS update is the only option.
guide.iommu.enable.option_missing.text: Can't find an IOMMU or VT-d option? Many boards only show it after a BIOS update, and some laptops hide it.
guide.iommu.enable.outcome: Did the IOMMU restriction go away?
guide.iommu.enable.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.iommu.enable.summary: Fixes the VAN RESTRICTION that asks for IOMMU by turning it on in the BIOS, and updating the BIOS if the option is missing. About 10-15 minutes.
guide.iommu.enable.title: Turn on IOMMU (VT-d / AMD-Vi)
guide.mouse.usb.accel.s1: Let VTDiag turn off mouse acceleration. You can undo it in VTDiag.
guide.mouse.usb.accel.s2: Open the Range and test your aim.
guide.mouse.usb.accel.text: 'Enhance pointer precision' is on. It changes how far the cursor moves depending on how fast you move, so aim feels floaty.
guide.mouse.usb.buttons.s1: In your mouse software, check the side buttons (Mouse 4 and Mouse 5).
guide.mouse.usb.buttons.s2: If one is set to 'Browser Back' or 'Forward', set it back to its default 'Mouse button 4/5'. Then bind it in VALORANT.
guide.mouse.usb.buttons.s3: Turn off macros and rapid-fire features. Don't use macros in VALORANT.
guide.mouse.usb.buttons.text: Clicks stop working after Alt-Tab, or a side button does strange things?
guide.mouse.usb.feel.s2: Turn off 'Optimizations for windowed games' and test again. This fixed the mouse feel for some players.
guide.mouse.usb.feel.s3: Check your mouse speed in Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Mouse too.
guide.mouse.usb.feel.text: Aim feels different since a Windows update?
guide.mouse.usb.outcome: Try aiming in the Range. Does your mouse feel normal now?
guide.mouse.usb.polling.s1: Open your mouse software (for example Logitech G HUB, Razer Synapse or SteelSeries GG).
guide.mouse.usb.polling.s2: Set the polling rate (or 'report rate') to 1000 Hz.
guide.mouse.usb.polling.s3: Using 4000 or 8000 Hz? That causes stutter on some PCs, so go back to 1000 Hz and test.
guide.mouse.usb.polling.s4: Wireless mouse: charge it. On some mice a low battery lowers the polling rate.
guide.mouse.usb.polling.text: The polling rate is how many times per second the mouse reports to the PC.
guide.mouse.usb.port.s1: Plug the mouse (or its wireless dongle) into a USB port on the back of the PC, straight on the motherboard.
guide.mouse.usb.port.s2: Don't use the front panel, a USB hub, the keyboard's port or the monitor's USB ports for the mouse.
guide.mouse.usb.port.s3: Still lagging? Try another back port; some mice work better on a USB 3 port (often blue), some on USB 2.
guide.mouse.usb.port.s4: Wireless: keep the dongle close to the mouse, ideally within 20 cm. Use the extension cable or dock that came with the mouse to put it on the desk.
guide.mouse.usb.port.s5: Mouse drops out for a moment? Let VTDiag stop Windows from putting USB ports to sleep.
guide.mouse.usb.port.text: The USB port matters more than you'd think.
guide.mouse.usb.summary: Mouse lag or skipping usually comes from the USB port, the wireless dongle's distance, the polling rate or mouse software settings. About 5 minutes.
guide.mouse.usb.title: Fix mouse lag, stutter or clicks that stop
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.not_x3d.s1: Check your processor in Settings > System > About ('Processor'). If its name doesn't end in 'X3D', or your board isn't MSI, this guide isn't for you.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.not_x3d.text: This option only exists on MSI boards with AMD X3D processors.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.outcome: Stay in the VALORANT lobby for a few minutes. Did the freezes stop?
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.pre.0: BitLocker is on. Changing BIOS settings can make Windows ask for your BitLocker recovery key. Save it first: click Start, type 'Manage BitLocker', open it and choose 'Back up your recovery key'.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.summary: On MSI motherboards with an AMD X3D processor, the BIOS option 'X3D Gaming Mode' turns off part of the processor. Some players had lobby freezes with it on. Reports are mixed, so treat it as a test. About 10 minutes.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.title: Turn off MSI 'X3D Gaming Mode'
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.x3d.s1: Open these steps on your phone first, because the PC screen will be in the BIOS. Change only the setting named here.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.x3d.s2: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If the BIOS doesn't open, restart and press {key} again and again while the PC starts.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.x3d.s3: In MSI's BIOS (Click BIOS), look for 'X3D Gaming Mode', often a button at the top of the start screen (EZ Mode). Can't see it? Press F7 for Advanced mode.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.x3d.s5: Press F10 to save and exit, then confirm with 'Yes'.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.x3d.s6: Start VALORANT and stay in the lobby for a few minutes.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.x3d.s7: No difference? Turn it back on the same way, then check the other guides in your report.
guide.msi_x3d.game_mode.x3d.text: You have an AMD X3D processor. Turn the option off for a test.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.outcome: Play one match with WARP on. Is your ping lower and steadier now?
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.pre.0: Your PC is losing packets even to your own router. Fix your home connection first (see 'Make your home connection steady'); WARP can't fix that part.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.server_wide.s1: Open status.riotgames.com, choose VALORANT and your region.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.server_wide.s2: If Riot lists a problem there, it's on their side. Waiting is the fix; you don't need to change anything on your PC.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.server_wide.s3: If Riot shows nothing, it can be your internet provider's route. Try the WARP steps in the next part.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.server_wide.te: Your friends on the same server have the same problem. Then it may be Riot or a big provider, not your PC.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.summary: If your home network is fine but your ping to Riot is still high or you lose packets, the problem is often the route your internet provider uses. The free 1.1.1.1 app can send your traffic another way. About 10 minutes.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.tell_isp.s1: Write down when it happens (date and time), which VALORANT server you play on (for example Istanbul or Frankfurt) and your ping.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.tell_isp.s2: Also write your ping with WARP off and with WARP on. A big difference shows the route is the problem, not your PC.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.tell_isp.s3: Save the VTDiag report and take a screenshot of your ping in the game.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.tell_isp.s4: Contact your internet provider's support and say: ping to the game server is high only through your network and normal over another route. Ask them to check the route.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.tell_isp.s5: If many players in your area have it, it is often fixed within a few days. Use WARP while you wait.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.tell_isp.s6: If nothing changes and friends on other providers are fine, you can also send the same notes to Riot Player Support.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.tell_isp.text: The real fix for a bad route is on your internet provider's side. Telling them helps everyone near you.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.title: Get around a bad internet route with Cloudflare WARP
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.warp.s1: First, write down your ping. In VALORANT turn on Settings > Video > Stats > 'Network Round Trip Time', then play a Deathmatch.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.warp.s2: Download the free '1.1.1.1' app from Cloudflare's official site (one.one.one.one) and install it.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.warp.s3: Open it, make sure the mode is 'WARP' (not only '1.1.1.1'), and turn the big switch on.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.warp.s4: Start VALORANT and play the same mode. Compare your ping and packet loss with your note.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.warp.s5: Better? Keep WARP on only while you play, and turn it off after.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.warp.s6: Not better, or worse? Turn WARP off and quit it (right-click its icon next to the clock > Quit), so it doesn't keep running for nothing.
guide.net.cloudflare_warp.warp.text: WARP sends your traffic through Cloudflare's network, which can skip a broken route. It's free. Your ping may go up a few ms, or drop a lot if the route was bad.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.dns.s2: Click 'Ethernet' or 'Wi-Fi' (the one you use). For Wi-Fi, open your network's properties or 'Hardware properties'.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.dns.s3: Next to 'DNS server assignment', click 'Edit' and choose 'Manual'.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.dns.s4: Turn on IPv4. Preferred DNS: 1.1.1.1, Alternate DNS: 1.0.0.1. (Google's are 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4.)
guide.net.dns_ipv6.dns.s5: Click 'Save', then restart the Riot Client.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.dns.s6: To undo it later, set 'DNS server assignment' back to 'Automatic (DHCP)'.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.dns.text: Your provider's DNS can be slow or send you to the wrong voice server. A public DNS from Cloudflare or Google is free and often more reliable.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.flush.s1: Let VTDiag clear the DNS cache. It's harmless; Windows rebuilds it by itself.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.flush.s2: Close the Riot Client fully (right-click its icon next to the clock > Exit) and open it again.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.flush.text: Start with the quickest step: clear Windows' saved list of internet addresses.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.ipv6.s1: Let VTDiag turn off IPv6 only on the connection you use. You can undo it in VTDiag.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.ipv6.s2: Restart the Riot Client and try again.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.ipv6.s3: Have 'Killer Intelligence Center' or 'Killer Control Center'? Open it and turn off its traffic prioritization, or update the Intel/Killer network driver.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.ipv6.text: Some network cards (like Killer) and some providers handle IPv6 badly, which breaks voice chat or causes VAL 57 / 59. Turning IPv6 off on your connection is safe; the internet keeps working over IPv4.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.outcome: Join a match. Does voice chat work and is the error gone?
guide.net.dns_ipv6.summary: Voice chat that won't connect, or VAL 57 / 59 errors, often come from your provider's DNS or from IPv6. These changes are small and easy to undo. About 5 minutes.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.title: Fix voice chat and VAL 57 / 59 with DNS and IPv6
guide.net.dns_ipv6.voice_checks.s1: In VALORANT Settings > Audio > Voice Chat, check that 'Output Device' and 'Input Device' are your headset and mic.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.voice_checks.s2: Turn Party and Team voice off in the lobby, play a round, then turn them on again. This helped some players.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.voice_checks.s3: Close overlays like Discord's or NVIDIA's (see 'Close overlays and recording programs', guide.apps.close_overlays).
guide.net.dns_ipv6.voice_checks.s4: If nobody on your server has voice, it may be on Riot's side. Check status.riotgames.com.
guide.net.dns_ipv6.voice_checks.s5: Cloudflare WARP fixed voice chat for some players (see guide.net.cloudflare_warp).
guide.net.dns_ipv6.voice_checks.text: If voice chat still doesn't work, check these.
guide.net.local_connection.cable.s1: Connect a network (Ethernet) cable from a free port on the router to the PC. A long, flat cable works fine.
guide.net.local_connection.cable.s2: Windows uses the cable by itself once it's plugged in.
guide.net.local_connection.cable.s3: While you play on cable, turn Wi-Fi off (network icon next to the clock > Wi-Fi tile) so Windows can't jump between them.
guide.net.local_connection.cable.s4: Can't run a cable? Powerline adapters (internet over the power sockets) or a mesh Wi-Fi point near the PC are options, but they cost money.
guide.net.local_connection.cable.text: A network cable is always steadier than Wi-Fi. It's the single best thing you can do for ping.
guide.net.local_connection.general.s1: Restart the router: unplug its power for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
guide.net.local_connection.general.s2: Pause downloads and updates on your PC (Steam, Epic, Windows Update, OneDrive).
guide.net.local_connection.general.s3: Ask the people at home if they stream or download big files while you play.
guide.net.local_connection.general.s4: Notice when it happens. Lag only in the evening usually means a busy network or provider, not your PC.
guide.net.local_connection.general.s5: Still lagging on cable with a quiet network? See the guide 'Get around a bad internet route with Cloudflare WARP' (guide.net.cloudflare_warp).
guide.net.local_connection.general.text: General checks for a steadier connection.
guide.net.local_connection.outcome: Play one match. Are the lag spikes and packet loss gone?
guide.net.local_connection.router.s1: Restart the router: unplug its power for 30 seconds, plug it back in and wait 2 to 3 minutes.
guide.net.local_connection.router.s2: On cable: check both ends are clicked in. Try another cable or another port on the router.
guide.net.local_connection.router.s3: Ask if someone is downloading or streaming while you play. A full connection makes your ping jump (this is called bufferbloat).
guide.net.local_connection.router.s4: Pause downloads on your own PC too: Steam, Epic, Windows Update, OneDrive, torrents.
guide.net.local_connection.router.s5: If your router has a 'QoS' or 'gaming' setting, turning it on can keep ping steady when others use the internet.
guide.net.local_connection.router.s6: Still losing packets on cable? The router may be old or faulty, so ask your internet provider to check or replace it.
guide.net.local_connection.router.text: Your PC loses packets even to your own router, so the problem is inside your home, not at Riot.
guide.net.local_connection.summary: Most lag spikes and packet loss start between your PC and your router. A cable, the right Wi-Fi band and a quiet network fix most of it. 5 to 15 minutes.
guide.net.local_connection.title: Make your home connection steady
guide.net.local_connection.two_connectio: Let VTDiag turn off the connection you're not using. You can undo it any time.
Cable and Wi-Fi are both connected. Windows can jump between them in the middle of a match.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_24.s1: Click the network icon next to the clock and open the Wi-Fi list.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_24.s2: Look for your network's name with '5G' or '5GHz' at the end, and connect to that one.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_24.s3: Only one name? Many routers mix both bands; staying closer usually makes the PC pick 5 GHz.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_24.s4: To check the band, open Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > your network's properties and look at 'Network band'.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_24.s5: No 5 GHz network at all? Ask whoever manages the router to turn it on (very old Wi-Fi cards may not support it).
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_24.text: You're on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. It reaches far but is slower and crowded (neighbors, Bluetooth, microwaves). 5 GHz is much better for games when you're not too far away.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_weak.s1: Best fix: use a network cable from the router to your PC. See the 'cable' part below.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_weak.s2: No cable? Move the PC or the router closer, ideally in the same room.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_weak.s3: Put the router up high and in the open, not in a cabinet, behind the TV or on the floor.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_weak.s4: Keep metal things, mirrors and fish tanks out of the way between the PC and the router.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_weak.s5: On a desktop with a Wi-Fi card, make sure its antennas are screwed on and pointing up.
guide.net.local_connection.wifi_weak.tex: Your Wi-Fi signal is weak. Walls, floors and distance eat the signal, and that causes lag spikes.
guide.network.firewall.allow.s2: Click 'Firewall & network protection' > 'Allow an app through firewall', then 'Change settings'.
guide.network.firewall.allow.s3: Find 'Riot Client', 'VALORANT' and 'Vanguard' or 'vgc' in the list. Tick both 'Private' and 'Public' for each.
guide.network.firewall.allow.s4: One is missing? Click 'Allow another app' > 'Browse' and pick it from: C:\Riot Games\Riot Client\RiotClientServices.exe and C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard\vgc.exe.
guide.network.firewall.allow.s5: The game itself is usually C:\Riot Games\VALORANT\live\ShooterGame\Binaries\Win64\VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe (on another drive, use that letter).
guide.network.firewall.allow.s6: Click OK and restart the Riot Client. Keep the firewall itself on.
guide.network.firewall.allow.text: Make sure Windows Firewall allows the three Riot programs on every network type.
guide.network.firewall.block_rules.s1: Click Start and type 'Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security', then open it.
guide.network.firewall.block_rules.s3: Look for rules with a red circle icon whose name or program mentions Riot, VALORANT or vgc.
guide.network.firewall.block_rules.s4: Right-click each one > 'Disable Rule'. Disabling is safer than deleting; you can turn it back on.
guide.network.firewall.block_rules.s6: Close the window and restart the Riot Client.
guide.network.firewall.block_rules.text: VTDiag found firewall rules that block Riot programs. Old tweaks or 'block internet' tools often leave these behind.
guide.network.firewall.outcome: Open the Riot Client. Does it download and connect now?
guide.network.firewall.summary: If the firewall blocks the Riot Client, VALORANT or Vanguard, downloads get stuck or the game can't connect. You'll allow these programs; the firewall stays on. About 10 minutes.
guide.network.firewall.third_party.s1: Open your security program (its icon is next to the clock).
guide.network.firewall.third_party.s2: Find 'Firewall' or 'Network protection', then 'Program rules', 'Application rules' or 'Traffic rules'.
guide.network.firewall.third_party.s3: Set the Riot Client (RiotClientServices.exe), VALORANT and Vanguard (vgc.exe) to 'Allow'.
guide.network.firewall.third_party.s4: Don't turn the firewall off. If you can't find the setting, see 'Stop your antivirus from blocking Riot' (guide.av.exclusions).
guide.network.firewall.third_party.text: You have another security program. Many of them (Norton, Kaspersky, ESET, Bitdefender and others) bring their own firewall, which replaces Windows' one.
guide.network.firewall.title: Let Riot through the firewall
guide.performance.basics.background.s1: Close what you don't need: browser tabs with videos, other launchers, downloads, recording.
guide.performance.basics.background.s2: Turn on Game Mode: Settings > Gaming > Game Mode.
guide.performance.basics.background.s3: Let VTDiag switch to the High performance power plan.
guide.performance.basics.background.s4: On a laptop, plug in the charger and see 'Make your laptop run at full speed' (guide.power.laptop_mode).
guide.performance.basics.background.text: Free up the PC for the game.
guide.performance.basics.caps.s1: In VALORANT Settings > Video > Stats, turn on 'Client FPS' so you can see it.
guide.performance.basics.caps.s2: In Settings > Video > General, turn 'Limit FPS Always' off, or set it above your monitor's refresh rate.
guide.performance.basics.caps.s3: 'Limit FPS in Menu' and 'in Background' can stay low (30 to 60). It doesn't affect matches and keeps the PC cooler.
guide.performance.basics.caps.s4: Check the NVIDIA app or AMD Software doesn't set a 'Max Frame Rate', 'Frame Rate Target Control' or 'Radeon Chill' for VALORANT.
guide.performance.basics.caps.s5: Turn V-Sync off in the game unless you use G-Sync or FreeSync (see guide.display.settings).
guide.performance.basics.caps.text: Start with the FPS limits. A low limit can hide your real FPS.
guide.performance.basics.honest.s1: VALORANT needs a good processor more than a strong graphics card.
guide.performance.basics.honest.s2: Videos showing very high FPS are often in the empty Range. Real matches with 10 players give less.
guide.performance.basics.honest.s3: Older 2 or 4-core processors, 8 GB RAM or very old laptops have a real limit. No setting can remove it.
guide.performance.basics.honest.s4: Low settings give the most FPS: Material, Texture and Detail on Low, Anti-Aliasing off.
guide.performance.basics.honest.s5: Still very low on good hardware? Check the other causes in your VTDiag report.
guide.performance.basics.low_ram.s1: Close the browser and other apps while you play.
guide.performance.basics.low_ram.s2: 16 GB (2 x 8 GB) is the comfortable amount for VALORANT today. Upgrading costs money, so only if you can.
guide.performance.basics.low_ram.text: You have less than 16 GB of RAM. VALORANT plus Discord and a browser can fill 8 GB, and then the PC slows down.
guide.performance.basics.one_stick.s1: Check in Task Manager > Performance > Memory: 'Slots used' shows how many sticks you have.
guide.performance.basics.one_stick.s2: This costs money: add a second stick that matches (same size and speed), or buy a 2-stick kit.
guide.performance.basics.one_stick.s3: Put them in the slots your motherboard manual says (usually the 2nd and 4th from the processor).
guide.performance.basics.one_stick.s4: Laptops: some have one free slot, others have RAM soldered on. Check your model first.
guide.performance.basics.one_stick.text: You have one RAM stick. With two matching sticks ('dual channel') the processor gets about twice the memory speed, and VALORANT can gain a lot of FPS.
guide.performance.basics.outcome: Play one match. Is your FPS better now?
guide.performance.basics.ssd.s1: Open Task Manager > Performance and click each disk. Under the name it says 'SSD' or 'HDD'.
guide.performance.basics.ssd.s2: VALORANT is in C:\Riot Games by default. Check which disk that is.
guide.performance.basics.ssd.s3: On an HDD, and you have an SSD with enough free space (about 50 GB)? Uninstall VALORANT in the Riot Client and install it again on the SSD.
guide.performance.basics.ssd.text: VALORANT on a hard disk (HDD) loads slowly and can stutter.
guide.performance.basics.summary: If your FPS is lower than expected, check the simple things first: FPS limits, background apps, power, RAM setup and where the game is installed. 15 to 30 minutes. Some limits are just the hardware, and that's okay to know.
guide.performance.basics.title: Get the FPS your PC can really do
guide.performance.basics.xmp.s1: Check in Task Manager > Performance > Memory > 'Speed'. If it's much lower than on the RAM box (for example 2133 instead of 3200, or 4800 instead of 6000), the profile is off.
guide.performance.basics.xmp.s2: Open these steps on your phone first, because the PC screen will be in the BIOS. Change only the setting named here.
guide.performance.basics.xmp.s3: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If the BIOS doesn't open, restart and press {key} again and again while the PC starts.
guide.performance.basics.xmp.s4: Find 'XMP', 'EXPO' or 'DOCP' (often on the first BIOS page) and pick 'Profile 1'.
guide.performance.basics.xmp.s5: Press F10 to save and exit, then confirm with 'Yes'.
guide.performance.basics.xmp.s6: The first start can take a minute while the RAM is tested. Wait, don't turn it off.
guide.performance.basics.xmp.s7: If the PC won't start or crashes after this, it usually resets itself after a few tries. Then set the profile back to 'Disabled'.
guide.performance.basics.xmp.text: RAM runs at a slow default speed until you turn on its profile in the BIOS (XMP on Intel, EXPO on AMD, sometimes 'DOCP'). Many PCs come with it off.
guide.power.laptop_mode.battery.s1: Plug in the laptop's own charger. A phone USB-C charger usually can't give enough power for games.
guide.power.laptop_mode.battery.text: Your laptop is running on battery, so it slows itself down.
guide.power.laptop_mode.gpu.s1: Let VTDiag tell Windows to run VALORANT on the graphics card.
guide.power.laptop_mode.gpu.s2: Some laptops have a 'dGPU only', 'Ultimate' or 'Discrete' mode in the maker's app. It's faster but needs a restart and uses more battery.
guide.power.laptop_mode.gpu.text: Your laptop has two graphics chips. Make sure VALORANT uses the strong one.
guide.power.laptop_mode.outcome: Play one match plugged in. Is your FPS better now?
guide.power.laptop_mode.power_mode.s2: Set 'Power mode' to 'Best performance' (while plugged in).
guide.power.laptop_mode.power_mode.text: Windows 11 also has a 'Power mode' setting.
guide.power.laptop_mode.pre.0: Your laptop is on battery. Plug in the charger first; most laptops limit speed on battery.
guide.power.laptop_mode.saver_plan.s1: Let VTDiag switch to the High performance power plan. You can undo it in VTDiag.
guide.power.laptop_mode.saver_plan.text: Windows uses a power-saving plan that slows the processor down.
guide.power.laptop_mode.summary: Laptops save power by slowing down, especially on battery or in quiet mode. Plugging in and picking the right modes can double your FPS. About 5 minutes.
guide.power.laptop_mode.title: Make your laptop run at full speed
guide.power.laptop_mode.vendor_app.s1: Lenovo: open Lenovo Vantage (or Legion Space) and pick 'Performance' or 'Extreme Performance'. On Legion laptops Fn+Q switches modes.
guide.power.laptop_mode.vendor_app.s2: ASUS: open Armoury Crate and set 'Operating Mode' to 'Performance' or 'Turbo' (often Fn+F5).
guide.power.laptop_mode.vendor_app.s3: MSI: open MSI Center > 'User Scenario' and pick 'Extreme Performance'.
guide.power.laptop_mode.vendor_app.s4: HP: open OMEN Gaming Hub > 'Performance Control' and pick 'Performance'.
guide.power.laptop_mode.vendor_app.s5: The fans will get louder. That's normal and means the laptop is cooling itself.
guide.power.laptop_mode.vendor_app.s6: Keep the maker's app updated (Microsoft Store > Library > Get updates, or the maker's site). An old Lenovo Vantage version slowed Wi-Fi down while VALORANT ran; a newer one fixed it.
guide.power.laptop_mode.vendor_app.text: Gaming laptops have their own app with a performance mode. It often matters more than Windows' settings.
guide.riot.client_repair.outcome: Does the Riot Client update and start VALORANT now?
guide.riot.client_repair.reinstall.s1: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps and uninstall VALORANT.
guide.riot.client_repair.reinstall.s2: Open File Explorer, go to C:\Riot Games (or the drive where you installed it) and delete the 'Riot Client' folder, plus the VALORANT folder if it's still there.
guide.riot.client_repair.reinstall.s3: Download the official installer from playvalorant.com and run it.
guide.riot.client_repair.reinstall.s4: Restart when Vanguard asks, then sign in and play.
guide.riot.client_repair.reinstall.text: The last step if Repair and the cache reset didn't help. It's a big download (tens of GB), so do it when you have time.
guide.riot.client_repair.repair.s1: Open the Riot Client. Click your profile icon (top right) > Settings.
guide.riot.client_repair.repair.s2: Click VALORANT on the left, then Repair. Wait until it's done.
guide.riot.client_repair.repair.s3: Close the Riot Client fully (arrow ^ next to the clock > right-click Riot Client > Exit) and open it again.
guide.riot.client_repair.repair.text: Repair checks every VALORANT file and downloads only what's broken. It's safe and keeps your settings.
guide.riot.client_repair.summary: Fixes broken game files, update loops and 'Something went wrong' errors in the Riot Client. Start with Repair (5-15 minutes); a full reinstall is the last step.
guide.riot.client_repair.title: Repair the Riot Client and VALORANT
guide.riot.client_repair.update_loop.s1: Close the Riot Client fully: arrow (^) next to the clock > right-click the Riot Client icon > Exit.
guide.riot.client_repair.update_loop.s2: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc). If you still see 'Riot Client' processes, right-click them > End task.
guide.riot.client_repair.update_loop.s3: Press Win+R, paste this and press Enter.
guide.riot.client_repair.update_loop.s4: Delete only the folder named 'Riot Client' there. Don't touch any other folder.
guide.riot.client_repair.update_loop.s5: Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
guide.riot.client_repair.update_loop.s6: Open the Riot Client, sign in again and let it update.
guide.riot.client_repair.update_loop.tex: Stuck on 'Updating', or getting an error right after an update? The client's own cache is probably broken. Removing it only signs you out; your game and account are safe.
guide.riot.client_settings.hw_accel.s1: Open the Riot Client settings (profile icon > Settings) and look for 'Hardware acceleration', usually under General.
guide.riot.client_settings.hw_accel.s3: Close the Riot Client fully (arrow ^ next to the clock > right-click Riot Client > Exit) and open it again.
guide.riot.client_settings.hw_accel.s4: Play a match and see if the stutter is gone.
