guide.riot.client_settings.hw_accel.text: The Riot Client uses your graphics card to draw its own window. On some PCs that causes stutter or a frozen client, and turning it off helps.
guide.riot.client_settings.summary: Covers 'Failed to launch' from unaccepted terms, stutter from the client's hardware acceleration, and the game not opening from a shortcut. A few minutes each.
guide.riot.client_settings.terms.s1: In the Riot Client, click your profile icon > Sign out.
guide.riot.client_settings.terms.s3: Read and accept the Terms window when it appears.
guide.riot.client_settings.terms.text: 'VALORANT failed to launch - something unusual happened' can simply mean new Terms of Service are waiting and the popup didn't show up.
guide.riot.client_settings.title: Fix Riot Client launch problems
guide.riot.client_settings.tray_launch.s: Click the arrow (^) next to the clock. If the Riot Client icon is there, click it and press Play in the client.
If that doesn't work: right-click the Riot Client icon > Exit. Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and end any leftover 'Riot Client' tasks.
Start the Riot Client from the Start menu instead of an old desktop shortcut, and press Play.
If the old shortcut is broken, delete it. Make a new one: Start > type Riot Client > right-click > Pin to taskbar.
Vanguard just installed or updated? Restart the PC once (Restart, not Shut down).
Still nothing? Let VTDiag set the Riot Client to run as administrator. You can undo it.
guide.riot.client_settings.tray_launch.t: Nothing happens when you click the shortcut? The Riot Client may already be running hidden in the tray, or the shortcut is broken.
guide.riot.server_status.friends_too.s1: Open status.riotgames.com, choose VALORANT and your region, and look for current incidents or maintenance.
guide.riot.server_status.friends_too.s2: If there's an incident, wait until it's marked as resolved. Reinstalling or changing settings won't help.
guide.riot.server_status.friends_too.s3: Restart the Riot Client after the incident is over.
guide.riot.server_status.friends_too.s4: No incident listed but many people have it? Check Riot's official VALORANT support accounts for news, then try again later.
guide.riot.server_status.friends_too.tex: Your friends have the same problem right now, so it's almost certainly Riot's servers or a big internet provider issue, not your PC.
guide.riot.server_status.slow_download.s: In the Riot Client, pause the download, wait 10 seconds and resume it. This often connects you to a faster server.
Close other downloads and streams (Steam, Windows Update, videos) while it runs.
Restart the Riot Client, or try again later; night or early morning is often faster.
Some players get a faster route with the free Cloudflare WARP (1.1.1.1) app. Turn it off again before you play.
If it stays slow for days, check status.riotgames.com and contact Riot support.
guide.riot.server_status.slow_download.t: Downloading at about 1 MB/s even though your internet is fast? Riot's download servers are sometimes slow for a while.
guide.riot.server_status.status.s1: Open status.riotgames.com, choose VALORANT and your region, and look for current incidents or maintenance.
guide.riot.server_status.status.s2: If an incident is listed, wait until it's resolved, then restart the Riot Client.
guide.riot.server_status.status.s3: Ask a friend in your region whether they have it too.
guide.riot.server_status.status.s4: If Riot reports nothing and only you have it, go back to VTDiag's other results.
guide.riot.server_status.status.text: A black screen at match start, chat that doesn't work, or login errors that come and go can be Riot-side incidents.
guide.riot.server_status.summary: Some problems are on Riot's side, like outages or slow download servers. Check the status page and wait; there's nothing to fix on your PC. A few minutes.
guide.riot.server_status.title: Check if it's a Riot server problem
guide.riot.support_ticket.hwid_ban.s1: Read Riot's page 'Understanding Hardware ID (HWID) Bans' on support.riotgames.com.
guide.riot.support_ticket.hwid_ban.s2: If you think it's a mistake, open a ticket and ask for a review. Each account needs its own ticket.
guide.riot.support_ticket.hwid_ban.s3: Be honest and stay polite. Riot reviews it, but there's no guarantee.
guide.riot.support_ticket.hwid_ban.s4: Some restrictions end on a set date. Then waiting until that date is the only way.
guide.riot.support_ticket.hwid_ban.s5: Never use 'HWID spoofers' or ban bypass tools. They break Riot's rules, often contain malware and lead to longer bans.
guide.riot.support_ticket.hwid_ban.text: VAN 152 (or VAL 61) means a ban, not a PC problem: Riot restricted this device or account after a rules check. No setting, reinstall or tool can lift it.
guide.riot.support_ticket.outcome: Did you manage to send the ticket?
guide.riot.support_ticket.summary: When the problem is on Riot's side or nothing else helped: collect logs with Riot's free Repair Tool and open a ticket with your VTDiag report. About 10 minutes.
guide.riot.support_ticket.ticket.s1: Download the Riot Repair Tool (RRT). It's free, from Riot's support site: go to support.riotgames.com and search 'Riot Repair Tool'.
guide.riot.support_ticket.ticket.s2: Right-click it > Run as administrator. Choose VALORANT and let it finish. It saves a .zip file with logs and tells you where.
guide.riot.support_ticket.ticket.s3: Save your VTDiag report with the Export button.
guide.riot.support_ticket.ticket.s4: Go to support.riotgames.com > VALORANT > Submit a ticket and sign in with your Riot account.
guide.riot.support_ticket.ticket.s5: Write the exact error (for example VAN 9003), when it started and what you already tried. Attach the RRT .zip and the VTDiag report.
guide.riot.support_ticket.ticket.s6: Send logs only to Riot support, never post them publicly. They can contain account details.
guide.riot.support_ticket.ticket.s7: Riot answers by email, so check your spam folder too. Reply in the same ticket instead of opening new ones.
guide.riot.support_ticket.ticket.text: Riot support can see things VTDiag can't, like account restrictions or server problems. Good logs make their answer much faster.
guide.riot.support_ticket.title: Contact Riot support
guide.runtimes.install.directx.s1: On microsoft.com, find 'DirectX End-User Runtimes (June 2010)' and download it.
guide.runtimes.install.directx.s2: Run it. It asks for a folder to unpack into: make a new, empty folder (for example on the desktop) and pick it.
guide.runtimes.install.directx.s3: Open that folder and run DXSETUP.exe. Follow the steps.
guide.runtimes.install.directx.s4: Also install both Visual C++ files (X64 and X86) from Microsoft's 'latest supported downloads' page.
guide.runtimes.install.directx.s6: Don't download single DLL files from 'DLL download' sites, and don't delete DLLs from Windows folders. The Microsoft installers put the right files in place.
guide.runtimes.install.directx.text: Errors with XINPUT1_3.dll or other DirectX files come from old DirectX parts that Windows doesn't include by default. Install the Visual C++ runtimes too if you haven't.
guide.runtimes.install.n_edition.s1: Windows 11: open Settings > System > Optional features and click 'View features' next to 'Add an optional feature'.
guide.runtimes.install.n_edition.s2: Windows 10: open Settings > Apps > Optional features > 'Add a feature'.
guide.runtimes.install.n_edition.s3: Search 'Media Feature Pack', tick it and install.
guide.runtimes.install.n_edition.text: You have a Windows 'N' edition, which comes without media parts. VALORANT needs them.
guide.runtimes.install.outcome: Restart your PC and start VALORANT. Is the error gone?
guide.runtimes.install.summary: Errors like 'side-by-side configuration is incorrect', XINPUT1_3.dll or other missing DLLs mean some free Microsoft parts are missing or broken. Installing them from Microsoft fixes it. About 10 minutes.
guide.runtimes.install.system_files.s1: Open an admin Command Prompt: click Start, type cmd, right-click 'Command Prompt' > 'Run as administrator' > Yes.
guide.runtimes.install.system_files.s2: Paste this command and press Enter. It can take 10 to 20 minutes.
guide.runtimes.install.system_files.s3: Then paste this one and press Enter. Wait until it reaches 100%.
guide.runtimes.install.system_files.s4: Restart your PC and start VALORANT.
guide.runtimes.install.system_files.text: If it still fails, Windows' own files may be damaged. These are Microsoft's standard repair tools.
guide.runtimes.install.title: Install the Microsoft parts VALORANT needs
guide.runtimes.install.vcredist.s1: Search 'Visual C++ Redistributable latest supported downloads' and open the page on microsoft.com.
guide.runtimes.install.vcredist.s2: Download both files: 'X64' (vc_redist.x64.exe) and 'X86' (vc_redist.x86.exe). You need both, even on 64-bit Windows.
guide.runtimes.install.vcredist.s3: Run each one. If it says it's already installed, click 'Repair'.
guide.runtimes.install.vcredist.text: The Microsoft Visual C++ runtimes are missing or broken.
guide.secureboot.enable.boot_failed_afte: Hold the power button until the PC turns off. Turn it on and tap {key} again and again to open the BIOS.
Only to get back into Windows for now: set Secure Boot back to Disabled (and CSM back to Enabled if you changed it). Press F10 and choose Yes.
If Windows asks for a BitLocker recovery key, type it in. You can find it on your phone at aka.ms/myrecoverykey (sign in with your Microsoft account).
Back in Windows, let VTDiag check your disk type. If it says MBR, that was the reason: do the MBR part of this guide first.
If the disk is GPT, update your BIOS first (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide). Older BIOS versions often have Secure Boot bugs.
Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
Open the Secure Boot page ({secureboot}). Under Key Management choose 'Restore Factory Keys' (or 'Install Default Secure Boot Keys'), then set Secure Boot to Enabled.
Press F10 and choose Yes. If the PC still won't start, turn Secure Boot off again the same way and contact Riot support with your VTDiag report.
Your PC stopped starting (or showed a Secure Boot error) after you turned Secure Boot on. Your files are almost always fine. First get back into Windows, then fix the real reason and try again.
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.s1: First let VTDiag check the disk. If it says MBR, do the MBR part first, or Windows won't start in UEFI mode.
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.s2: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.s3: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.s4: If the BIOS opens in a simple screen, switch to 'Advanced Mode' (often F7 or F2).
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.s5: Set CSM (or 'Legacy Support') to Disabled and Boot Mode to UEFI. Then set Secure Boot to Enabled. Usually here: {secureboot}
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.s6: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.s7: If Windows doesn't start, go back into the BIOS and turn CSM back on to get in. Nothing is lost; the disk most likely needs the MBR conversion first.
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.s8: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check Secure Boot again.
guide.secureboot.enable.csm.text: Your PC starts Windows in the old Legacy (CSM) mode. Secure Boot needs pure UEFI mode, so CSM has to be turned off.
guide.secureboot.enable.general.s1: Let VTDiag check the disk type. If it says MBR, use the MBR part first, otherwise Windows may not start after the change.
guide.secureboot.enable.general.s2: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.secureboot.enable.general.s3: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.secureboot.enable.general.s4: Set Boot Mode to UEFI, CSM/Legacy to Disabled and Secure Boot to Enabled. Usually here: {secureboot}
guide.secureboot.enable.general.s5: If Secure Boot is grey or says 'Setup Mode', open Key Management and choose 'Restore Factory Keys' or 'Install Default Secure Boot Keys'.
guide.secureboot.enable.general.s6: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.secureboot.enable.general.s7: If Windows doesn't start, go back into the BIOS and undo the change (CSM on, Secure Boot off) just to get in. Then check the disk type first.
guide.secureboot.enable.general.s8: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check Secure Boot again.
guide.secureboot.enable.general.text: Not sure what state your PC is in? This path checks first, then walks you through the BIOS change safely. You can also look yourself: Start > 'System Information' > 'BIOS Mode' should be UEFI and 'Secure Boot State' should be On.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.s1: Back up your important files (photos, documents, saves) to a USB stick or the cloud. The conversion normally keeps everything, but a backup is the safe way.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.s2: If BitLocker or Device encryption is on: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Suspend protection. Save your recovery key too.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.s3: Open an admin Command Prompt: press Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator. Click Yes.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.s4: Paste this test command and press Enter; it changes nothing. If it doesn't end with 'Validation completed successfully', stop here and ask Riot support for help.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.s5: Only if the test passed: paste this to convert the disk. This is one-way, and Windows won't start again until you switch the BIOS to UEFI in the next step.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.s6: Right away, click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows tries to start instead, restart and tap {key} again and again.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.s7: Set Boot Mode to UEFI, CSM/Legacy to Disabled and Secure Boot to Enabled. Usually here: {secureboot}. Then press F10 and choose Yes.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.s8: When Windows is back, resume BitLocker if you suspended it (Manage BitLocker > Resume protection) and let VTDiag check Secure Boot.
guide.secureboot.enable.mbr.text: Your Windows disk uses the old MBR layout. Secure Boot only works with the newer GPT layout, so the disk must be converted first. Windows has a free built-in tool for this (MBR2GPT).
guide.secureboot.enable.outcome: Did VALORANT start without the Secure Boot error (VAN 9003 / RESTRICTION)?
guide.secureboot.enable.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.secureboot.enable.sb_on_still_fail: Let VTDiag confirm that Secure Boot is really on.
Install all Windows updates and restart. Microsoft delivers the new 2023 Secure Boot certificates through Windows Update.
Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
Keep Secure Boot Enabled. Under Key Management choose 'Restore Factory Keys' or 'Install Default Secure Boot Keys' ({secureboot}), then press F10 and choose Yes.
If your BIOS is old, update it (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide). New BIOS versions bring new Secure Boot keys.
Still the same error? Open VTDiag's guide 'Secure Boot is on, but Vanguard can't verify it'.
If nothing helps, contact Riot support with your VTDiag report (VTDiag's 'Contact Riot support' guide).
Windows already reports Secure Boot as On, but Vanguard still complains. Then it's usually the Secure Boot keys, Microsoft's 2023 certificate update or a Riot-side check, not a switch you forgot.
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.s1: If BitLocker is on, keep your recovery key ready (aka.ms/myrecoverykey). Windows may ask for it once after this change.
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.s2: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.s3: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.s4: Open the Secure Boot page. Usually here: {secureboot}
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.s5: If needed, set Secure Boot Mode to Custom so Key Management appears. Choose 'Restore Factory Keys' or 'Install Default Secure Boot Keys' and confirm with Yes.
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.s6: If the BIOS asks whether to exit or reset now without saving, choose No. Set Secure Boot Mode back to Standard and Secure Boot to Enabled.
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.s7: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.s8: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check again. If your BIOS had no key option at all, update the BIOS first (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide).
guide.secureboot.enable.setup_mode.text: Your Secure Boot keys are missing (the BIOS is in 'Setup Mode'), so Secure Boot can't really switch on. Restoring the factory keys fixes this. They come from your PC maker and are safe.
guide.secureboot.enable.summary: Fixes VAN 9003 and VAN RESTRICTION 1/4 by turning on Secure Boot in the BIOS, after checking that your disk and boot mode are ready for it. Usually 10-20 minutes; longer if the disk needs converting.
guide.secureboot.enable.title: Turn on Secure Boot
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.s1: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.s2: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.s3: If the BIOS opens in a simple screen, switch to 'Advanced Mode' (often F7 or F2).
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.s4: Find Secure Boot and set it to Enabled. Usually here: {secureboot}
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.s5: If Secure Boot is grey or says 'Setup Mode', open Key Management, choose 'Restore Factory Keys' or 'Install Default Secure Boot Keys' and confirm with Yes.
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.s6: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.s7: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check Secure Boot again.
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.s8: Start VALORANT. If the error is still there, restart once more (Restart, not Shut down) and try again.
guide.secureboot.enable.uefi_sb_off.text: Your PC already runs in UEFI mode; Secure Boot just isn't switched on. This is usually a 5-minute change in the BIOS.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.attestation: Update graphics, chipset and storage drivers with your PC or motherboard maker's tools, or the graphics card maker's app.
Unplug USB devices you don't need (extra controllers, adapters, capture cards) and restart.
Test in the Range or a custom game first, so a failed start doesn't hurt you in a ranked or normal match.
Still failing? Open a Riot support ticket with your VTDiag report and the Riot Repair Tool logs (VTDiag's 'Contact Riot support' guide).
VAN 9101 means Vanguard couldn't fully verify your PC's current state. Riot's steps for it are about drivers, extra devices and background software.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.ca2023_miss: Install all Windows updates and restart. Do it twice; the certificate update can need more than one restart.
Open Windows Security > Device security and look at the Secure Boot part. If it says an update or action is needed, do what it says.
Let VTDiag check the certificate again.
Still missing? Update your BIOS (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide). New BIOS versions include the 2023 certificates.
Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
Keep Secure Boot Enabled and choose 'Restore Factory Keys' or 'Install Default Secure Boot Keys' ({secureboot}). Press F10 and choose Yes.
Back in Windows, let VTDiag check again.
Your PC's Secure Boot list doesn't have Microsoft's new 2023 certificate yet. Windows Update and newer BIOS versions add it.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.outcome: Did the Secure Boot policy / attestation error go away?
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_off.s1: Let VTDiag check Secure Boot once more.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_off.s2: If it's still off, open VTDiag's 'Turn on Secure Boot' guide and come back here only if the error stays afterwards.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_off.text: Secure Boot is actually off on your PC. Turn it on first with VTDiag's 'Turn on Secure Boot' guide; this guide is for when it's already on.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_on.s1: Install all Windows updates and restart.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_on.s2: Open Windows Security > Device security and check the Secure Boot part for a warning or a pending update.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_on.s3: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_on.s4: Riot's official fix for this error: keep Secure Boot Enabled and choose 'Restore Factory Keys' or 'Install Default Secure Boot Keys' ({secureboot}). Press F10 and choose Yes.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_on.s5: If your BIOS is older than about a year, update it (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide).
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_on.s6: Check status.riotgames.com and Riot's support site. If many players have it, a small Riot Client update often fixes it; restart the client to get it.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_on.s7: Still stuck? Open a Riot support ticket with your VTDiag report and your PC model (VTDiag's 'Contact Riot support' guide). Riot sometimes needs the model to fix it.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.sb_on.text: Secure Boot is on, but Vanguard says it can't verify the Secure Boot policy. In 2026 this hit many players at once, and part of it was fixed on Riot's side.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.summary: For VAN STATUS_SB_POLICY, VAN RESTRICTION 1 with Secure Boot already on, and VAN 9101. Often linked to Secure Boot certificate updates or a Riot-side issue. 15-30 minutes of updates; sometimes it needs a fix from Riot.
guide.secureboot.policy_wave.title: Secure Boot is on, but Vanguard can't verify it
guide.shader_cache.warmup.clear.s2: Click Start, type 'Disk Cleanup' and open it. Pick drive C:.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.clear.s3: Tick 'DirectX Shader Cache' (you can untick the rest) and click OK > 'Delete Files'.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.clear.s4: Start VALORANT and warm up again. The first matches stutter again; that's expected.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.clear.s5: Do this only once when needed, not every day.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.clear.text: If the stutter doesn't get better after a few matches, the saved shaders may be broken. Clearing them is safe; they get built again.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.drivers.s1: Don't switch drivers back and forth every day. Pick one and give it a few matches.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.drivers.s2: If one new driver keeps stuttering even after warming up, go back one version with a clean install (guide.gpu.clean_driver) and stay there.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.drivers.s3: AMD: leave Anti-Lag and AFMF (Fluid Motion Frames) off for VALORANT.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.drivers.s4: Close RivaTuner and other overlays too (guide.apps.close_overlays).
guide.shader_cache.warmup.drivers.text: Every driver change resets the shaders, so jumping between drivers keeps the stutter coming back.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.outcome: After a few matches, is the stutter gone?
guide.shader_cache.warmup.summary: After a new graphics driver or a VALORANT update, the graphics card has to build its 'shaders' (small programs for effects) again. Until then the first matches can stutter. This is normal and goes away. 10 to 30 minutes of playing.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.title: Stop stutter after a driver or game update
guide.shader_cache.warmup.warmup.s1: Open the Range for 5 to 10 minutes. Walk around and use a few agents' abilities.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.warmup.s2: Play 1 to 3 Deathmatch or unrated games.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.warmup.s3: The stutter should get less with each match.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.warmup.s4: NVIDIA: leave 'Shader Cache Size' at 'Driver Default' in NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D settings. Don't set it to 'Disabled'.
guide.shader_cache.warmup.warmup.text: Give the game a little time to build the shaders.
guide.standby_memory.basics.s1: Restart before you play: Start > Power > 'Restart'. 'Shut down' with Fast Startup doesn't fully clear memory.
guide.standby_memory.basics.s2: Close memory-hungry apps: browsers with many tabs, Discord video, other launchers.
guide.standby_memory.basics.s3: Open Task Manager > Processes and click 'Memory' to sort. See what uses the most.
guide.standby_memory.basics.s4: If memory use keeps rising for hours even with apps closed, a program or driver has a 'memory leak'. Restart, and update your graphics driver and apps.
guide.standby_memory.islc.s1: Download ISLC from Wagnardsoft's official site and run it as administrator.
guide.standby_memory.islc.s2: Set 'The list size is at least' to 1024 MB.
guide.standby_memory.islc.s3: Set 'Free memory is lower than' to about half your RAM (for example 8192 for 16 GB).
guide.standby_memory.islc.s4: Leave 'Wanted timer resolution' unticked, then click 'Start'.
guide.standby_memory.islc.s5: No difference after a few days? Close and uninstall it; it wasn't the problem.
guide.standby_memory.islc.text: Optional: ISLC (Intelligent Standby List Cleaner) is a free tool by Wagnardsoft. It frees 'standby' memory when free memory runs low. Honestly, Windows usually handles this well; ISLC helps on some PCs and does nothing on others.
guide.standby_memory.low_ram.s1: 8 GB works for VALORANT, but it's tight with Discord and a browser open. Close them while you play.
guide.standby_memory.low_ram.s2: 16 GB (2 x 8 GB) is the comfortable amount today. Upgrading costs money, so only if you can.
guide.standby_memory.low_ram.text: You have less than 16 GB of RAM, so memory fills up fast.
guide.standby_memory.outcome: Restart and play a few matches. Is the stutter gone?
guide.standby_memory.summary: If VALORANT stutters more the longer the PC has been on, memory may be filling up. A restart and fewer open apps fix most of it. 5 minutes.
guide.standby_memory.title: Fix stutter from full memory
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.s1: Close everything Riot: click the small arrow (^) next to the clock, right-click the Riot Client icon > Exit. Then right-click the red Vanguard icon > Exit Vanguard.
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.s2: Open an admin Command Prompt: press Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator. Click Yes.
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.s3: Paste this and press Enter. When it says the drive is in use and asks to check at the next restart, type Y and press Enter.
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.s4: Restart. The check runs before Windows starts and can take from 30 minutes to a few hours. Don't turn the PC off.
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.s5: If Windows starts without checking (Vanguard blocked it), uninstall Riot Vanguard in Settings > Apps > Installed apps, then repeat the chkdsk command and the restart.
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.s6: When Windows is back, open an admin Command Prompt again, paste this and press Enter. It can take 10-20 minutes.
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.s7: Then paste this and press Enter. Restart when it's done.
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.s8: Open the Riot Client. If you removed Vanguard, it installs it again; restart when it asks.
guide.storage.chkdsk.dirty.text: Windows marked your disk as needing a check, but Vanguard starts so early that the check can't run. Exiting or briefly removing Vanguard lets Windows do it. Back up important files first if you can.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.s1: Close everything Riot: click the small arrow (^) next to the clock, right-click the Riot Client icon > Exit. Then right-click the red Vanguard icon > Exit Vanguard.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.s2: Open an admin Command Prompt: press Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator. Click Yes.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.s3: Paste this and press Enter. When it says the drive is in use and asks to check at the next restart, type Y and press Enter.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.s4: Restart. The check runs before Windows starts and can take from 30 minutes to a few hours. Don't turn the PC off.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.s5: If Windows starts without checking (Vanguard blocked it), uninstall Riot Vanguard in Settings > Apps > Installed apps, then repeat the chkdsk command and the restart.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.s6: When Windows is back, open an admin Command Prompt again, paste this and press Enter. It can take 10-20 minutes.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.s7: Then paste this and press Enter. Restart when it's done.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.s8: Open the Riot Client. If you removed Vanguard, it installs it again; restart when it asks.
guide.storage.chkdsk.general.text: Use this if Windows keeps saying a disk needs repair, or if system or game files seem corrupt. Back up important files first if you can.
guide.storage.chkdsk.outcome: Did the disk check run, and is the problem gone?
guide.storage.chkdsk.pre.0: Close VALORANT and the Riot Client first.
guide.storage.chkdsk.summary: Lets Windows repair the disk and system files when Vanguard keeps blocking the disk check. About 30 minutes to a few hours, mostly waiting.
guide.storage.chkdsk.title: Check and repair the disk
guide.storage.intel_vmd.outcome: Did VALORANT start without VAN STATUS_VMD_9001?
guide.storage.intel_vmd.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.pre.1: Plug in the charger first. A BIOS or firmware update must never run on battery power.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.riot_support.s1: Use VTDiag's 'Contact Riot support' guide to send your report and logs.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.riot_support.s2: Mention your PC model and the exact error: VAN STATUS_VMD_9001.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.riot_support.s3: Meanwhile, install the newest Intel RST driver from your PC maker (the first part of this guide).
guide.storage.intel_vmd.riot_support.tex: Not sure this is your problem, or you'd rather not risk the BIOS change? That's a good call. Riot support can look at your case first.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.safe_first.s1: Find your model: Settings > System > About. On Dell, also note the Service Tag (on the sticker or in the Dell app).
guide.storage.intel_vmd.safe_first.s2: Open your maker's support site (Dell: dell.com/support), enter the model or Service Tag and go to Drivers.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.safe_first.s3: Download and install the 'Intel Rapid Storage Technology' driver for your exact model, then restart.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.safe_first.s4: Start VALORANT. If you still get VAN STATUS_VMD_9001, contact Riot support with your VTDiag report before you change anything in the BIOS.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.safe_first.s5: Riot may have a fix or a specific instruction for your model. Only try the 'turn off VMD' part if Riot support can't help.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.safe_first.text: Riot's first fix is the right Intel Rapid Storage Technology (RST) driver from your PC maker. Try this before touching the BIOS.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.summary: Vanguard can't talk to the Intel VMD storage controller, which is common on Dell and Alienware. Start with the safe driver fix and Riot support; switching VMD off is risky and only for when nothing else works.
guide.storage.intel_vmd.title: Fix the Intel VMD error (VAN STATUS_VMD_9001)
guide.storage.intel_vmd.vmd_off_safemode: Open these steps on your phone and save your BitLocker recovery key (aka.ms/myrecoverykey). Then Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Suspend protection, so the BIOS change doesn't lock your disk.
Open an admin Command Prompt: press Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator. Click Yes.
Paste this and press Enter. It makes the next start go into Safe Mode.
Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
Find the VMD setting. On Dell it's usually Storage > 'SATA/NVMe Operation': change 'RAID On' to 'AHCI/NVMe' (or turn off 'Enable VMD Controller'). Apply, then Exit.
Windows now starts in Safe Mode (black background); that's expected. Open an admin Command Prompt, paste this and press Enter.
Restart. Windows should now start normally.
If you get a blue screen at any point: go back into the BIOS, set it back to 'RAID On', start Windows and run the command from the Safe Mode step again. Then contact Riot support.

This turns off Intel VMD in the BIOS. Without the Safe Mode trick below, Windows can't find its disk afterwards and shows a blue screen, so follow every step in order. Only do this after the safe part.
guide.tpm.enable.general.s2: You can check yourself: press Start, type tpm.msc and press Enter. It should say 'The TPM is ready for use' and Specification Version 2.0.
guide.tpm.enable.general.s3: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.tpm.enable.general.s4: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.tpm.enable.general.s5: Turn the TPM on. Usually here: {tpm}
guide.tpm.enable.general.s6: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.tpm.enable.general.s7: Back in Windows, start VALORANT. If the error stays, try the other parts of this guide or contact Riot support.
guide.tpm.enable.general.text: Not sure what's wrong with the TPM? Check first, then turn it on in the BIOS if needed.
guide.tpm.enable.no_tpm.s1: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.tpm.enable.no_tpm.s2: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.tpm.enable.no_tpm.s3: If the BIOS opens in a simple screen, switch to 'Advanced Mode' (often F7 or F2).
guide.tpm.enable.no_tpm.s4: Turn the TPM on. Usually here: {tpm}
guide.tpm.enable.no_tpm.s5: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.tpm.enable.no_tpm.s6: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check for TPM 2.0.
guide.tpm.enable.no_tpm.s7: Can't find any TPM, fTPM or PTT option? Update the BIOS first (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide) and look again. If it's still missing, read the 'TPM 1.2 / old hardware' part.
guide.tpm.enable.no_tpm.text: Windows can't see any TPM. On most PCs from about 2017 or newer, it's built into the processor (fTPM on AMD, PTT on Intel) and just switched off in the BIOS.
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.s1: Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.s2: Let VTDiag check the TPM again.
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.s3: You can check yourself: press Start, type tpm.msc and press Enter. It should say 'The TPM is ready for use' and Specification Version 2.0.
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.s4: Don't press 'Clear TPM' unless Riot or Microsoft support tells you to. It can remove your Windows PIN and trigger BitLocker recovery.
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.s5: Update your BIOS (VTDiag's 'Update your BIOS' guide). Older BIOS versions, especially on AMD, had fTPM bugs.
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.s6: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.s7: Make sure the TPM is still enabled: {tpm}. BIOS updates often switch it off. Press F10 and choose Yes.
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.s8: Still not ready? Contact Riot support with your VTDiag report.
guide.tpm.enable.not_ready.text: Windows sees a TPM, but it says it isn't ready. This often clears after a proper restart or a BIOS update.
guide.tpm.enable.outcome: Did the TPM error go away?
guide.tpm.enable.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.tpm.enable.summary: Fixes VAN 9001 / 9090 and TPM restrictions by turning on the security chip that is built into most processors (fTPM on AMD, PTT on Intel). About 10 minutes in the BIOS.
guide.tpm.enable.title: Turn on TPM 2.0
guide.tpm.enable.tpm12_only.s1: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.tpm.enable.tpm12_only.s2: Look for a firmware TPM: {tpm}. If you find fTPM, PTT or 'Firmware TPM', enable it and pick it instead of the 'Discrete' chip, then press F10 and choose Yes.
guide.tpm.enable.tpm12_only.s3: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check for TPM 2.0.
guide.tpm.enable.tpm12_only.s4: Prebuilt PC or laptop (Dell, HP, Lenovo...)? Look on its support page for a 'TPM firmware update' to 2.0 or a newer BIOS. Use only the maker's own tool.
guide.tpm.enable.tpm12_only.s5: Desktop motherboard? Check its manual for a TPM header (often labelled TPM, JTPM or SPI_TPM). If it has one, a TPM 2.0 module made for that exact board can be added.
guide.tpm.enable.tpm12_only.s6: A module costs money and isn't a sure fix: Riot says some restriction checks need the processor's built-in firmware TPM. Ask Riot support before you buy one.
guide.tpm.enable.tpm12_only.s7: If none of these exist, this PC's hardware can't meet the requirement. Contact Riot support with your VTDiag report, or play on another PC.
guide.tpm.enable.tpm12_only.text: Your PC has a TPM, but only the older version 1.2, and VALORANT needs 2.0. Some PCs can still get 2.0, but some older hardware simply can't. That's nobody's fault.
guide.valorant.config_reset.config_corru: Save your crosshair: in VALORANT go to Settings > Crosshair, use the export / copy profile code button and paste the code into Notepad.
Most settings are saved on your Riot account, but write down your sensitivity and important key binds just in case.
Close VALORANT and the Riot Client (arrow ^ next to the clock > right-click Riot Client > Exit).
Press Win+R, paste this and press Enter.
Right-click the 'Config' folder > Rename, and call it Config.old. Nothing is deleted, so you can undo this.
Start VALORANT. It creates a fresh Config folder. Check your settings and import your crosshair code.
Fixed? You can delete Config.old later. Not fixed? Close the game, delete the new Config and rename Config.old back to Config.
VTDiag found signs that VALORANT's local settings files are damaged.
guide.valorant.config_reset.general.s1: Save your crosshair: in VALORANT go to Settings > Crosshair, use the export / copy profile code button and paste the code into Notepad.
guide.valorant.config_reset.general.s2: Most settings are saved on your Riot account, but write down your sensitivity and important key binds just in case.
guide.valorant.config_reset.general.s3: Close VALORANT and the Riot Client (arrow ^ next to the clock > right-click Riot Client > Exit).
guide.valorant.config_reset.general.s4: Press Win+R, paste this and press Enter.
guide.valorant.config_reset.general.s5: Right-click the 'Config' folder > Rename, and call it Config.old. Nothing is deleted, so you can undo this.
guide.valorant.config_reset.general.s6: Start VALORANT. It creates a fresh Config folder. Check your settings and import your crosshair code.
guide.valorant.config_reset.general.s7: Fixed? You can delete Config.old later. Not fixed? Close the game, delete the new Config and rename Config.old back to Config.
guide.valorant.config_reset.general.text: Crashes on 'Graphics Quality', keys that act strangely, or settings that won't save are often caused by damaged local settings files.
guide.valorant.config_reset.outcome: Is the crash or the key problem gone?
guide.valorant.config_reset.pre.0: Close VALORANT and the Riot Client first.
guide.valorant.config_reset.summary: Fixes crashes when changing graphics settings, stuck or dead keys and other settings glitches by letting VALORANT rebuild its settings files. About 5 minutes, and it can be undone.
guide.valorant.config_reset.title: Reset VALORANT's local settings
guide.vanguard.precheck.not_sure.s1: Check your Windows version: Settings > System > About > Windows specifications > Version.
guide.vanguard.precheck.not_sure.s2: If it's older than 25H2, you can't have Pre-Check. Use the 'Pre-Check is off' part.
guide.vanguard.precheck.not_sure.s3: Still unsure? Open the red Vanguard icon in the tray (^ next to the clock) and look for the Pre-Check setting.
guide.vanguard.precheck.not_sure.s4: Only if Pre-Check is off: let VTDiag set vgc to Automatic.
guide.vanguard.precheck.not_sure.text: Not sure if you use Pre-Check? It only exists on Windows 11 version 25H2 or newer, and you have to turn it on yourself in the Vanguard menu. If you never changed it, you most likely don't use it.
guide.vanguard.precheck.outcome: Does VALORANT start without the Vanguard error now?
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_off.s1: Let VTDiag set the vgc service to Automatic and start it. You can undo this.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_off.s2: Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_off.s3: Let VTDiag check that vgc is running.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_off.s4: Start VALORANT. If the error is still there, try VTDiag's 'Reinstall Vanguard cleanly' guide.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_off.tex: Pre-Check is off, so Vanguard should start with Windows. If its 'vgc' service isn't set to Automatic, you get errors like VAL 79 or VAN 57. Riot's fix is to set it to Automatic.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_on.s1: Nothing is broken just because vgc is stopped while you aren't playing.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_on.s2: If you get a Vanguard error: click the small arrow (^) next to the clock and open the red Vanguard icon. It shows which requirement needs attention.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_on.s3: Pre-Check only works while Secure Boot, TPM 2.0, IOMMU and Memory Integrity are all on. Fix the one Vanguard names with VTDiag's matching guide.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_on.s4: To stop using Pre-Check: open the Vanguard menu from the tray, switch Vanguard Pre-Check off and restart the PC.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_on.s5: After turning Pre-Check off, vgc should start with Windows again. If it doesn't, use the 'Pre-Check is off' part of this guide.
guide.vanguard.precheck.precheck_on.text: You use Vanguard Pre-Check. Then Vanguard only starts when you open a Riot game, so the 'vgc' service being Manual and stopped is normal. Don't set it to Automatic.
guide.vanguard.precheck.summary: Explains Vanguard Pre-Check (Vanguard only runs while you play, on Windows 11 25H2 or newer) and when the 'vgc' service should be set to Automatic. 2-5 minutes.
guide.vanguard.precheck.title: Vanguard Pre-Check explained
Let VTDiag move this file to a safe place. It can be put back if needed.
Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
Open the Riot Client and start VALORANT.
Let VTDiag check that Vanguard's driver is running.
Vanguard left behind a boot status file that can make it think a restart is still needed. Moving it aside lets Vanguard create a fresh one.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.fast_startup: Let VTDiag turn off Fast Startup for you. You can undo it any time; starting the PC may take a few seconds longer.
Close VALORANT and the Riot Client.
Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
Open the Riot Client and start VALORANT.
Let VTDiag check that Vanguard's driver is running.
Fast Startup is on. With it, 'Shut down' doesn't really restart Windows, so Vanguard's driver never gets loaded. Only 'Restart' gives a real fresh start.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.general.s1: Save your work and close VALORANT and the Riot Client.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.general.s2: Click Start > Power > Restart. Use Restart, not Shut down.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.general.s3: Wait until Windows has fully started, then open the Riot Client and play.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.general.s4: Let VTDiag check that Vanguard's driver is running.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.general.s5: Still asked to restart every time? Try VTDiag's 'Reinstall Vanguard cleanly' guide.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.general.text: VAL 45 ('Vanguard reboot required') or VAN 57 usually just means Vanguard's driver isn't loaded yet. One real restart fixes most cases.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.outcome: After the restart, did VALORANT start without VAL 45 / VAN 57?
guide.vanguard.real_restart.stale_dat.s1: Let VTDiag move the old file to a safe place. It can be put back if needed.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.stale_dat.s2: Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
guide.vanguard.real_restart.stale_dat.s3: Open the Riot Client and start VALORANT.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.stale_dat.s4: Let VTDiag check that Vanguard's driver is running.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.stale_dat.te: An old Vanguard file from before the last update can cause crashes or 'restart required' loops. VTDiag can move it aside safely.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.summary: Fixes 'Vanguard reboot required' (VAL 45) and VAN 57 when Vanguard's driver didn't load. Takes 2-3 minutes.
guide.vanguard.real_restart.title: Restart properly (not Shut down)
guide.vanguard.reinstall.files_missing.s: Close everything Riot: click the small arrow (^) next to the clock, right-click the Riot Client icon > Exit. Then right-click the red Vanguard icon > Exit Vanguard.
Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps. Find 'Riot Vanguard', click the three dots > Uninstall and confirm.
If the uninstall fails or Riot Vanguard isn't listed: Open an admin Command Prompt: press Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator. Click Yes.

Paste this one too and press Enter.

Open File Explorer and go to C:\Program Files. If a 'Riot Vanguard' folder is still there, delete it.
Open the Riot Client. It installs Vanguard again by itself. When it asks you to restart, restart before you press Play.
guide.vanguard.reinstall.files_missing.t: Some Vanguard files or services are missing, so Vanguard can't start. A clean reinstall puts them back.

guide.vanguard.reinstall.pre.0: Close VALORANT and the Riot Client first.
guide.vanguard.reinstall.summary: Removes Riot Vanguard completely and lets the Riot Client install a fresh copy. Fixes install loops and broken-Vanguard errors (VAN -1, VAN 1067, VAN 83). About 10 minutes and two restarts.
guide.vanguard.reinstall.title: Reinstall Vanguard cleanly
Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager, then Performance > CPU. Look at the 'Virtualization' line.
If it says Enabled, you're done here. If it says Disabled, continue with the next steps.
Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
Set virtualization to Enabled. Usually here: {virtualization}
Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
Back in Windows, let VTDiag check again.
VTDiag couldn't tell for sure (Windows hides this when Memory Integrity is already running). Check it yourself first.
guide.virtualization.enable.off.s1: Open these steps on your phone first (scan the QR code). While the PC is in the BIOS, you can't see this window.
guide.virtualization.enable.off.s2: Click 'Restart into BIOS'. If Windows starts again instead, restart and tap {key} again and again right after the PC turns on.
guide.virtualization.enable.off.s3: If the BIOS opens in a simple screen, switch to 'Advanced Mode' (often F7 or F2).
guide.virtualization.enable.off.s4: Set virtualization to Enabled. Usually here: {virtualization}
guide.virtualization.enable.off.s5: If you see 'Execute Disable Bit' (Intel) or 'NX Mode' (AMD), make sure it's Enabled too.
guide.virtualization.enable.off.s6: Press F10 and choose Yes to save and exit (on some laptops: Apply, then Exit). The PC restarts.
guide.virtualization.enable.off.s7: Back in Windows, let VTDiag check again.
guide.virtualization.enable.off.s8: Next, turn on Memory integrity with VTDiag's 'Turn on Memory Integrity' guide, if Vanguard asks for it.
guide.virtualization.enable.off.text: CPU virtualization is switched off in the BIOS. AMD calls it SVM Mode, Intel calls it Intel Virtualization Technology (VT-x). Turning it on is safe and doesn't slow games down.
guide.virtualization.enable.outcome: Does Task Manager > Performance > CPU now show 'Virtualization: Enabled'?
guide.virtualization.enable.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.virtualization.enable.summary: Turns on the CPU virtualization switch in the BIOS. Memory Integrity and Vanguard's security checks need it. About 5-10 minutes.
guide.virtualization.enable.title: Turn on CPU virtualization (SVM / VT-x)
guide.vpn.remove.adapters.s1: Right-click the Start button and choose 'Device Manager'.
guide.vpn.remove.adapters.s3: Look for names like TAP-Windows, Wintun, WireGuard, VirtualBox Host-Only, VMware Network Adapter or Hamachi.
guide.vpn.remove.adapters.s4: Right-click each one > 'Disable device'. Don't uninstall; this way it's easy to turn back on.
guide.vpn.remove.adapters.s5: Don't touch your real Wi-Fi or Ethernet adapter (for example Realtek, Intel, Killer, MediaTek).
guide.vpn.remove.adapters.s6: Restart your PC and start VALORANT.
guide.vpn.remove.adapters.text: Uninstalled VPNs and virtual-machine programs can leave virtual network adapters behind.
guide.vpn.remove.outcome: Restart your PC and start VALORANT. Does it connect without the error now?
guide.vpn.remove.proxy.s2: Under 'Manual proxy setup', click 'Edit' (or 'Set up') next to 'Use a proxy server', turn it off and click 'Save'.
guide.vpn.remove.proxy.s4: If it turns itself back on, a program is setting it. Uninstall that program (see the 'uninstall' part).
guide.vpn.remove.proxy.s5: On a work or school PC, ask the IT person instead of changing it.
guide.vpn.remove.proxy.text: A proxy is set in Windows. Some 'free internet', unblocker or school tools set this.
guide.vpn.remove.service.s1: Let VTDiag stop the clashing program's service and keep it from starting with Windows.
guide.vpn.remove.service.s2: Restart your PC (Start > Power > Restart) and start VALORANT.
guide.vpn.remove.service.text: Easiest first step: stop the clashing program's background service. It stays installed.
guide.vpn.remove.summary: VPNs, proxies, other anti-cheats (like FACEIT) and virtual network adapters can block Vanguard and cause VAN errors or loading stuck at 20%. About 10 minutes plus a restart.
guide.vpn.remove.title: Turn off VPNs and programs that get in Vanguard's way
guide.vpn.remove.uninstall.s2: Look for VPN apps you don't use (for example NordVPN, Proton VPN, Hamachi, Radmin VPN, ZeroTier).
guide.vpn.remove.uninstall.s3: Look for other anti-cheats, like 'FACEIT AC' or 'ESEA'. You can reinstall FACEIT when you play CS again.
guide.vpn.remove.uninstall.s4: For each one, click '...' > Uninstall and follow the steps.
guide.vpn.remove.uninstall.s5: Work VPNs (like GlobalProtect) on a work or school PC: don't remove them, ask the IT person.
guide.vpn.remove.uninstall.s6: Docker Desktop or emulators: just quit them before you play.
guide.vpn.remove.uninstall.s7: Restart your PC and start VALORANT.
guide.vpn.remove.uninstall.text: Uninstall VPNs and other anti-cheats you don't need right now. You can install them again later.
guide.vpn.remove.vpn_on.s1: Find the VPN's icon next to the clock (click the ^ arrow to see hidden icons).
guide.vpn.remove.vpn_on.s2: Disconnect, then right-click the icon > 'Quit' or 'Exit'. Only disconnecting can leave its network filter running.
guide.vpn.remove.vpn_on.s4: Using Cloudflare WARP for a bad route? That's fine if it helps, but if you get a VAN error with it on, turn it off.
guide.vpn.remove.vpn_on.text: A VPN connection is active right now.
guide.wdfilter.reset.pre.0: BitLocker (drive encryption) is on. After BIOS or boot changes Windows may ask for the recovery key once, so save it first: Start > type 'Manage BitLocker' > Back up your recovery key. With a Microsoft account it's also at aka.ms/myrecoverykey.
guide.wdfilter.reset.pre.1: Close VALORANT and the Riot Client first.
guide.wdfilter.reset.reset_reinstall.s1: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps and uninstall VALORANT and Riot Vanguard. If Windows runs fine until you play, you can do this in normal Windows.
guide.wdfilter.reset.reset_reinstall.s2: If Windows crashes too often for that, use Safe Mode: Settings > System > Recovery > Advanced startup > Restart now > Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings > Restart, then press 4.
guide.wdfilter.reset.reset_reinstall.s3: If Vanguard won't uninstall, use the commands from VTDiag's 'Reinstall Vanguard cleanly' guide (sc delete vgc and sc delete vgk).
guide.wdfilter.reset.reset_reinstall.s4: Reset the Windows Security app: press Start, type Windows Security, right-click it > App settings > Reset.
guide.wdfilter.reset.reset_reinstall.s6: Install VALORANT again with the official installer from playvalorant.com. Restart when Vanguard asks.
guide.wdfilter.reset.reset_reinstall.s7: Keep Microsoft Defender on. Turning it off isn't a fix and leaves your PC unprotected.
guide.wdfilter.reset.reset_reinstall.s8: If WdFilter.sys bluescreens come back, contact Riot support with your VTDiag report and the crash code.
guide.wdfilter.reset.reset_reinstall.tex: Still crashing? Players fixed this by removing Riot's software, resetting the Windows Security app and installing Riot's software fresh.
guide.wdfilter.reset.summary: For bluescreens (PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA) that name WdFilter.sys while you play. Players fixed it by updating, then removing Riot software, resetting Windows Security and reinstalling. About 30-60 minutes.
guide.wdfilter.reset.title: Fix WdFilter.sys bluescreens
guide.wdfilter.reset.updates_first.s1: Install all Windows updates, including Defender updates, and restart.
guide.wdfilter.reset.updates_first.s2: Play for a while. If there are no more bluescreens, you're done. If they come back, use the next part.
guide.wdfilter.reset.updates_first.text: WdFilter.sys is part of Microsoft Defender, Windows' built-in antivirus. Start with updates: they fix many of these crashes.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.s1: Open Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates. Install everything, restart, and repeat until nothing new shows up.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.s2: If no newer Windows version is offered, go to Microsoft's official page microsoft.com/software-download. It's free.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.s3: If your PC supports Windows 11, use the 'Windows 11 Installation Assistant'. Otherwise use the Windows 10 Media Creation Tool (if Microsoft still offers it) and choose 'Upgrade this PC now'.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.s4: Pick the option that keeps your files and apps. Back up important files anyway, just to be safe.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.s5: Plug in the charger. The upgrade is a big download and can take 1-2 hours with several restarts.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.s6: Only use Microsoft's own site. 'Pre-activated' or modified Windows copies often break Vanguard.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.s7: Afterwards, press Start, type winver and press Enter to see your new version.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.s8: Let VTDiag check the Windows version.
guide.windows.update.below_22h2.text: You're on an older Windows 10 version. VALORANT may still start, but Riot asks for at least Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045) for some checks. Windows 10 no longer gets updates from Microsoft, so Windows 11 is the long-term fix if your PC supports it.
guide.windows.update.general.s1: Open Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates.
guide.windows.update.general.s2: Install everything that's offered and restart the PC.
guide.windows.update.general.s3: Check again and repeat until nothing new shows up.
guide.windows.update.general.s4: If an update keeps failing, write down its error code and search it on support.microsoft.com.
guide.windows.update.general.s5: Let VTDiag check the Windows version.
guide.windows.update.general.text: Keeping Windows up to date fixes many Vanguard errors (Riot lists it for VAN 0, 6, 84, 133 and others).
guide.windows.update.insider.s1: Open Settings > Windows Update > Windows Insider Program.
guide.windows.update.insider.s2: Turn on 'Stop getting preview builds'. On Beta or Release Preview, Windows then moves you back to normal Windows with the next big release.
guide.windows.update.insider.s3: Moved to the Insider build less than 10 days ago? Settings > System > Recovery > Go back may return you to your old Windows.
guide.windows.update.insider.s4: On Dev or Canary builds, the only quick way back is a clean install of normal Windows with the Media Creation Tool from microsoft.com/software-download. Back up your files first.
guide.windows.update.insider.s5: If the PC bluescreens with vgk.sys before you can do this, contact Riot support. Don't delete files in Windows folders by guessing.
guide.windows.update.insider.text: You're on a Windows Insider (preview) build. Vanguard often doesn't support brand-new preview builds yet, which causes vgk.sys bluescreens and errors.
guide.windows.update.kb5101650.s1: Open Settings > Windows Update > Update history. Scroll down and click Uninstall updates.
guide.windows.update.kb5101650.s2: Find KB5101650 in the list, click Uninstall and confirm.
guide.windows.update.kb5101650.s3: Restart the PC: Start > Power > Restart (not Shut down).
guide.windows.update.kb5101650.s4: Play a Deathmatch or a custom game and check if the microstutter is gone.
guide.windows.update.kb5101650.s5: If it didn't help, install the update again with Windows Update. It's a security update, so don't leave it off without a reason.
guide.windows.update.kb5101650.s6: If it helped, Windows may install it again later. You can pause updates for a week in Windows Update while Microsoft fixes it.
guide.windows.update.kb5101650.text: Players link Windows update KB5101650 (July 2026) to microstutter on alt-tab and when changing graphics settings. Removing it helped several of them, but Microsoft hasn't confirmed it.
guide.windows.update.outcome: Is Windows up to date, and does VALORANT run normally now?
guide.windows.update.pending_reboot.s1: Save your work. Click Start > Power > Update and restart (or Restart).
guide.windows.update.pending_reboot.s2: Let it finish. Don't turn the PC off while it says 'Working on updates'.
guide.windows.update.pending_reboot.s3: Let VTDiag check that nothing is waiting anymore.
guide.windows.update.pending_reboot.text: Windows has updates waiting for a restart. Vanguard checks can fail until that's done.
guide.windows.update.summary: Brings Windows to a version Vanguard supports, removes a known problem update, or leaves the Insider preview. Usually 15-60 minutes; a full version upgrade can take 1-2 hours.
guide.windows.update.title: Update Windows
guide.windows.update.too_old.s1: Open Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates. Install everything, restart, and repeat until nothing new shows up.
guide.windows.update.too_old.s2: If no newer Windows version is offered, go to Microsoft's official page microsoft.com/software-download. It's free.
guide.windows.update.too_old.s3: If your PC supports Windows 11, use the 'Windows 11 Installation Assistant'. Otherwise use the Windows 10 Media Creation Tool (if Microsoft still offers it) and choose 'Upgrade this PC now'.
guide.windows.update.too_old.s4: Pick the option that keeps your files and apps. Back up important files anyway, just to be safe.
guide.windows.update.too_old.s5: Plug in the charger. The upgrade is a big download and can take 1-2 hours with several restarts.
guide.windows.update.too_old.s6: Only use Microsoft's own site. 'Pre-activated' or modified Windows copies often break Vanguard.
guide.windows.update.too_old.s7: Afterwards, press Start, type winver and press Enter to see your new version.
guide.windows.update.too_old.s8: Let VTDiag check the Windows version.
guide.windows.update.too_old.text: Your Windows version is too old for Vanguard. Updating is free and keeps your files.

route.hardwareCannotComply.text: This hardware can't meet a Vanguard requirement. Settings won't change it; contact Riot support about your options.
route.hwidBanAppeal.text: This PC is banned by Riot (HWID restriction). There's nothing to fix on your PC, and no tool can change that. Only Riot's appeal process can.
route.riotServerIncident.text: Riot's servers have a problem or are in maintenance right now. Nothing on your PC needs fixing; check Riot's status page and try again later.
route.riotSupportTicket.text: Only Riot support can help with this. Send them a ticket with the logs from Riot's repair tool.
route.tryAnotherAccount.text: This error is often tied to your account, not your PC. Try a different Riot account on this PC: if it works, contact Riot support about your account.
route.unsupportedPlatform.text: This setup isn't supported by VALORANT (virtual machine, ARM processor, console or cloud gaming). No PC fix changes that.
rule.account-mfa-matchmaking-glitches.su: Login codes, linked accounts or matchmaking act strangely. These are account-side problems a PC tool can't fix; Riot support can.
rule.account-mfa-matchmaking-glitches.ti: An account or login problem on Riot's side

rule.amd-adrenalin-driver-regression.sum: Some AMD Adrenalin driver versions cause freezes, black screens and driver crashes in VALORANT. Rolling back to a stable version (clean install) fixes it; turning off extra Adrenalin features can help too.
